How To Get There: This place is 500mt south-east of Lodhauli (See map no.27E).

NOTE: The best route to reach Khanapur is vai Kaira (Khadiravana).

## 104 Khanapura (Khanpur)

After playing holi at Ranabadi, Radha and Krishna came here with the sakhas and sakhis and enjoyed a wonderful feast. The name of the village is derived from the word 'khana', which means any kind of meal like lunch or dinner or even a feast. The word 'khana' can also mean 'to eat food' as in 'khana kao' meaning 'please take your meal'.

How To Get There: This place is 3km east of Kaira (See map no.27E).

## 105 Umraya

It was here at Umraya on Magh-purnima that Shrimati Radharani was crowned the Queen of Vrindavana by Purnamasi Devi. In the Bhakti-ratnakara it is said, “Ordered by Lord Brahma who spoke from the sky, Purnamasi Devi crowned Radharani as the Queen of Vrindavana by jubilantly sprinkling the waters of the Manasi-ganga and other sacred rivers upon Her head.” The word, 'umraya' or 'raya' as well as 'umaraha', means a 'queen', 'a princess', or someone possessing 'great riches'. Because Radharani's crowning ceremony as the Queen of Vrindavana occurred here, that is how this village achieved its name of Umraya.

Umraya is the village where Lokanatha Goswami performed his bhajana and also the place where he discovered the Deity Radha-Vinoda hidden in the nearby Kishori-kunda. This kunda was very dear to Radharani, who is also known by the name of Kishori. Lokanatha Goswami was so renounced that he did not bother to build a kutira but simply lived under a tree. Whenever it rained he would put the Deity in the hollow of the tree and at other times he would keep the Deity in a bag hung around his neck. This Deity was later worshiped at the Gokulananda Mandira in Vrindavana, but due to an imminent attack by Aurangzeb on Vrindavana, the Deity was moved to Jaipura along with the other Deities of the Gaudiya Goswamis, where it is still being worshiped even today.

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “This beautiful Kishori-kunda is very dear to Kishori, the daughter of Vrishabhanu. Seeing this wonderful place, Lokanatha Goswami felt great pleasure within and resided here. There is no end to speaking of his renunciation. Shri Radha-Vinoda bestowed Their mercy on him here. Whenever he got fruits, roots, sak, or rice, Lokanatha Goswami would offer it to Shri Radha-Vinoda with great devotion. During the rainy and winter seasons Lokanatha stayed under this tree with only an old quilt and very old outer cloth. During the rains, Lokanatha would keep his Lord within the hollow of a tree and he would remain outside getting wet. At other times, he would happily keep Radha-Vinoda in an old bag hanging on his chest. Remembering the pastimes of Shri Gauracandra, he would become overwhelmed and cry at this place. After describing these topics Raghava became impatient and swam in his own tears. Shrinivasa and Narottama fell to ground and rolled in the dust. They sighed deeply and swam in their tears of ecstatic love. After some time Raghava Pandita regained his composure and, taking Shrinivasa and Narottama along, they continued on their way.”

How To Get There: This place is 2.5 km south of Khanpur (See map no.27E).

## 106 Ranabadi (Ra nwari)

This is where Radharani along with the gopis came to play holi with Krishna and the cowherd boys. The Holi-mela celebrations are known as the 'festival of colors' where revelers throw colored powder and colored water on each other. The holi festivities turned into a veritable battle with red colored gulal powder flying in all directions. Because the holi celebrations appeared like a battle between the cowherd girls and the cowherd boys, the village became known as Ranabadi, or the place of the battle. The word 'rana' can mean both a 'king' as well as a 'battle'.

How To Get There: This place is 4km north-east of Umraya and 4km south-west of Chhata (See map no.27E).

## 107 Chhatravana (Chhata)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “O Shrinivasa, see before us Chatravana. At this place the son of Nanda became king.” Chhatravana is mentioned in the Vraja-bhakti-vilas as being one of the upavanas (sub-forests) of Vrindavana Dhama. While playing at Chhatravana, Krishna, with the help of His cowherd boyfriends like Madhumangala and Subala, declared Himself as the 'King of the Forests' and ordered that no one could pick flowers without His permission. Meanwhile, some of the gopis were out picking flowers when they heard the news that some usurper had declared Himself the ruler over the kingdom reigned over by their own queen Srimati Radharani.

When the sakhis heard that Krishna had been crowned as the 'chatra-pati' or 'king of Vraja' by the cowherd boys at Chhatravana, they informed Lalita Devi who became furious. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “Lalita Devi became very, very angry and said, “Who is that person who claims authority over Radhika’s kingdom? We will immediately retaliate against this impostor.” The gopis then ran to inform Radharani, who had earlier been crowned 'Umraya', or 'Queen of Vraja' by none other than Purnamasi, after she was personally ordered to do so by Lord Brahma. At the suggestion of Her friends, Radharani demanded that the usurper be brought before Her to be punished. After receiving the queen's order, Lalita and the other gopis prepared for battle by arming themselves with flower-stick weapons specially made by Vrinda Devi.

Unaware of what was about to happen, the cowherd boys Madhumangala, Subala, Arjuna, Bhringa, Kokila, and Lavanga, were out picking flowers in the fields near Chhatravana when they were suddenly surprised to see thousands of gopis descend upon them from all directions. Subala and the others managed to escape but Madhumangala was immediately arrested and his hands bound behind his back with a flower garland. He was then marched off by the gopis who brought him before their queen for punishment. On seeing Krishna's friend Madhumangala brought before Her, Radharani repeatedly chided him for declaring a usurper as the 'king of Vrindavana' and told him that the real authority over this kingdom was now going to punish him. Bowing his head in submission Madhumangala said, “Give me such a punishment that my belly should be filled”. Hearing Madhumangala's reply, Radharani said, “Release this useless brahmana who is simply interested in filling his stomach and let him run to his king.” On being released and with his hands still bound-up, Madhumangala ran off to tell Krishna what had happened.

Meanwhile Krishna was sitting on His throne acting just like an arrogant king while surrounded by His doting and submissive subjects in the form of the cowherd boys. Madhumangala arrived there in a sorry condition with his hands still bound behind him. Madhumangala then told Krishna. “Just see, this is the result I get by declaring You as the king.” The real authority in these forests is the great and noble queen named Radharani, who has unlimited power and no one can dare stand against Her supreme authority. That same Cupid, who steals the composure of the world, trembles at the mere movement of Her lotus eyes. My only advice is that You must bow to Her authority, surrender Yourself completely, and take shelter of Her lotus feet.”

Hearing the sound advice of Madhumangala, His brahmana friend, Krishna untied his hands while saying He was extremely sorry that Madhumangala had to suffer such humiliation. Madhumangala told Krishna that it doesn't matter that he was insulted; his only interest was in serving Krishna and caring for His welfare. He then took Krishna's hand and led Him to the village of Umraya where the beautiful Queen Radharani was sitting with Her courtiers. Upon seeing Her beloved Krishna arrive in utter submission before Her royal assembly, Radharani immediately became shy and somewhat restless and wanted to remove Her royal robes, but the sakhis forbade Her to do so.

When Krishna saw His beloved Radharani in the dress of a queen, He became ecstatic and showed symptoms of being unsteady and restless. Madhumangala was thrilled to see Krishna respond to Radha's presence in such a way and led Him foreword to stand near to Her. Madhumangala then arranged for Radha and Krishna to sit down next to each other on the throne and then turning to Radharani he said. “You may now take this servant of Yours and show Your authority over Him and He will present You with a gift of His jewel-like embrace, please accept it with care.” Hearing these wonderful words of Madhumangala, the gopis were extremely happy and Lalita stepped forward and put a tasty laddu in Madhamangala's mouth. Madhumangala then told Lalita and the gopis, “You did wrong in binding me up, but if you can feed me with a hundred thousand laddus like this one, you can easily be freed from your offence.” All those assembled became ecstatic upon seeing Queen Radharani sitting in the loving embrace of Krishna. The 'divine lovers' Radha and Krishna then entered a nearby forest grove where They were served by Their faithful companions.

How To Get There: This place is 4km north-east of Ranwari. Chhata is on the Agra to Delhi road 28km north of Vrindavana (See map no.27E).

## 108 Bhandagora (Badali/Bhadawal)

It is said that the name of this village is derived from the word 'bandara' which means 'storeroom' or 'warehouse', because Nanda Maharaja kept one of his storehouses at this place. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “See here is Bhandagora-grama. O Shrinivasa, Krishna performed wonderful pastimes here. People now call this town Bhadali. One who takes bath here achieves all perfection.”

How To Get There: This place is 2.5km west of Chhata (See map no.27E).

## 109 Dhanasinga (Dhamsingha)

This is the village of the gopi Dhanishtha who is mentioned as being one of Krishna's personal maidservants and is engaged in service around Nanda Baba's house in Nandagrama, as well as in the kitchen helping mother Yashoda. She would also escort Radha to Her secret meetings with Krishna at Gupta-kunda. The name of this village has been derived from the name of Dhanishtha and in the village one can see Dhanishtha-kunda.

How To Get There: This place is 3km north of Bhadawal (See map no.27E).

## 110 Bhadravana

At this place the gopis dressed Krishna in a very attractive way with various ornaments and jewelry before taking Him to meet Radharani. The word 'bhadra' means 'attractive' and because Krishna was dressed very attractively (bhadra) by the gopis, this forest (vana) achieved its name. This particular Bhadravana forest is not one of the twelve sacred forests of Vraja; the original Bhadravana is located some distance from here on the eastern bank of the Yamuna River.

How To Get There: This place has not been located.

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 49 Yavat (Jao)

The Vraja-ritti-cintamani says, “This town of Yavata was built by Maharaja Vrsabhanu for the pleasure of His daughter. Radharani would often sit on the roof of Her palace at Yavat and gaze in the direction of Her lover’s home at Nandagrama, and in the same way Krishna would gaze in the direction of Yavata”. The ancient name of the village is derived from the word 'yava' or 'yavaka', which means the bright red pigment which is known in English as 'vermilion', or 'red lac'. The word 'vata' means a 'banyan tree'. In other words, this is the site under the shade of this famous banyana tree, where Krishna would secretly meet His beloved Radha and where He also applied yavaka on the soles of Radha's lotus feet. It is also said that the gopis also used to decorate Radha's lotus feet with yavaka under this same tree. Yavat is also mentioned in the Vishnu Purana as one of the adhivanas or sub-forests of Vrindavana where there is a sacred vata-vriksa or banyan tree known as Yavaka-vata. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “O Shrinivasa, this is the village of Yavat where Krishna meets with Radharani to enjoy amusement. Her sister-in-law, Kutila, and mother-in-law, Jatila, are not able to see Krishna, who is extremely clever. There is no limit to the happiness of their pastimes! Those who are greatly fortunate relish these pastimes in various ways.”

Yavata is the ancestral village of Abhimanyu, who is the supposed husband of Radharani. After Her marriage, Radharani moved from Her father's palace at Varsana to Yavata to live in Abhimanyu's house with his mother Jatila and sister Kutila. Due to Abhimanyu being somewhat dull-brained and backward, he did not know anything about marital relations and therefore the marriage with Radha was never consummated. Both Jatila and Kutila kept a watchful eye over Radharani due to persistent rumors that She was having an affair with Her childhood sweetheart Krishna. Regardless, Krishna regularly visited Yavata and expertly dressing Himself in various costumes and disguises would enter the house of Abhimanyu and enjoy transcendental pastimes with Radharani and Her girlfriends. Sometimes Krishna would even disguise Himself as Abhimanyu and after entering the house, inform mother Jatila that the cunning debauchee named Krishna was planning to come there disguised as her son. As soon as the real Abhimanyu arrived at his home, he suddenly found himself being abused with foul words, beaten over the head with a stick, and driven away by his own mother, much to the satisfaction of all the gopis, who took great pleasure in seeing such amazing and incredible pastimes. In the Bhakti-ratnakara it says, “O Shrinivasa, see here the enchanting Yao-grama known as Yavat, where many pastimes were performed. This is the residence of Abhimanyu where Radharani enjoyed playing with Her girlfriends. By the influence of Yogamaya, what to speak of touching Radharani Herself, Abhimanyu is not even able to touch Her shadow. He remains in the association of the cowherd men while Jatila and Kutila are always engaged in household work. The gopis cleverly bring Krishna here and their hearts become filled with joy as they witness the 'divine couple's' pastimes.”

The sakhis and the sakhas would often collaborate together in order to secretly smuggle Krishna into Jatila's house at Yavat, so they could all relish the amorous exchanges between Radha and Krishna. Once, mother Yashoda was planning to send a trunk full of expensive clothing and jewelry as a gift to Radharani. When Yashoda went to call Abhimanyu to carry the trunk to Yavat, seizing the opportunity, Krishna quickly hid inside the trunk along with the clothes and jewelry. Mother Yashoda then helped Abhimanyu place the trunk on his head and he carried it all the way to Yavata. On arriving at Yavata, Abhimanyu's mother Jatila, told him that the trunk containing gifts for Radharani should be put in Her bedroom. When Radha and Her girlfriends went to the bedroom and opened the trunk, they became ecstatic to find their beloved Krishna hiding inside.

## Yavat - Birthplace of the Manjaris

According to local legend, Yavat is also the birthplace of the eight principle manjaris who are the most intimate young friends of Radharani including: Rupa-manjari, Rati-manjari, Rasa-manjari, Manjulali-manjari, Guna-manjari, Vilasa-manjari, Kasturi-manjari, and Labanga-manjari. These manjaris are differentiated from the other gopis as they are all kaumaris, or pre-pubescent young girls, and can therefore enter the nikunja where Radha and Krishna are engaged in conjugal love and serve Them unhindered because they are not aroused or agitated with the desire to enjoy personally with Krishna. This creates an uninhibited atmosphere for the 'divine couple' to fully submerge themselves in one another's love without any distraction. The special feature of the manjaris is that they have given up their own opportunity to enjoy intimate pastimes with Krishna, simply so they can unreservedly render serve to the lotus feet of Radharani and help Her to fulfill Her own desires in Her conjugal relationship with Her beloved Krishna. Therefore, the manjaris are considered to be most spiritually advanced amongst the gopis of Vraja.

## There Are Three Types of Gopis

The Vedic shastras divide the gopis into three distinct categories: The first group are those gopis who are more inclined towards Krishna; referred to in Shrila Rupa Goswami's Ujvala Nilamani as Krishna-snehadika sakhis - or those gopi friends who have great love for Krishna. The second group are those gopis who are equally inclined towards both Radha and Krishna; referred to in Ujvala Nilamani as sama-sneha sakhis - or those gopi who love both Radha and Krsna equally. The third group are those gopi who are more inclined towards Radharani, referred to in Ujvala Nilamani as Priya-sakhyam snehadhika sakhis - or those gopis who have absolutely selfless love for Radha. This third category of gopi friends; the sakhyam snehadhika sakhis, are those who are in the mood of being manjaris and are exclusively the maidservant of Radharani. The manjaris have absolutely no desire whatsoever to become nayikas or intimate lovers of Krishna like the other gopis. The sole purpose of a manjaris existence is to see Radharani happily engaged in amorous pastimes with Her beloved Krishna.

The manjaris assist Radharani in meeting Krishna without any ulterior motive or thoughts regarding personal gain for themselves. Their primary activity is to decorate Radharani in various ways in order that She can attract the attention of Krishna and thus compel him to spend time with Her at a secret meeting place within the hidden bowers of Vrindavana's forests. The manjaris derive immense transcendental pleasure by uniting the 'divine lovers' and in this way they play an integral part in the superlative pastimes of parakiya-lila. The manjaris like Rupa Manjari, Rati Manjari Rasa-manjari and others, are attached to the exclusive service of Radharani and derive great happiness in seeing the 'divine couple' enjoying conjugal bliss. They are not concerned with anything other than this form of devotional service.

Shrila Narottama Das Thakura describes the mood of the manjaris in his book Prem Bhakti Chandrika, “Shri Rupa Manjari, Rati Manjari, Lavang Manjari, Manjulali Manjari and Ras Manjari, eagerly and lovingly serve Radharani, supplying Her with musk and various other articles. I am the follower of all these gopis. I shall serve them with great love. I will completely understand their orders, even when hidden in casual hints or gestures. I shall become immersed in wonder at their divine virtues and beauty, and I shall dearly love them. I shall always remain in their company. Immersed in the happiness of serving the 'divine couple’ surrounded by Their friends in Vrindavana, understanding the subtle hints of these gopis, taking up the chamar wisk, I will fan the 'divine couple’ and after that I will place betel nuts in Their moon-like mouths.”

## Philosophical Considerations Regarding Parakiya-rasa

When Radha's father Vrishabhanu Maharaja, under the guidance of Gargamuni and Purnamasi, married his daughter to Abhimanyu, it marked the beginning of the topmost super-excellent phase of Krishna's pastimes in Vraja known as the parakiya-rasa, which is the pinnacle of all rasa and gives Krishna the highest level of transcendental pleasure. This parakiya-rasa can only be experienced by Krishna and the gopis headed by Radharani, whereas the queens at Dwaraka headed by Rukmini, although they also enjoy the super-excellent madhurya-rasa or a conjugal relationship with Krishna as His wives, they cannot experience the exalted emotions of parakiya-bhava. This is because when lovers marry and live together at home, there are no feelings of separation and the expectation of meeting one's lover is also lost; being replaced with a feeling of happiness, fulfillment, and complete contentment (sambhanda). But, if through unforeseen circumstances, one's lover marries another person, the lovers then experience the bhava, or mood of separation (vipralambha); consequently meeting together becomes extremely difficult and can only be undertaken in secrecy. This greatly heightens the anticipation and expectation of meeting one's lover, as well as the intense pleasure derived from such a meeting, thus adding another level of pleasure to the relationship between lovers, not found in marriage. Therefore, the parakiya-rasa of love in separation is superior to all other rasas due to the intensity of the emotions experienced by the lovers.

Another important consideration is that all the nitya-siddha devotees who descended along with Krishna to assist Him in enjoying transcendental pastimes on earth, are all expansions of Krishna's own internal potency known as hladini-shakti, including all the gopis and gopas. Concomitantly, Abhimanyu is also one of Krishna's hladini-shakti expansions for the purpose of facilitating the ecstatic pastimes between Radha and Krishna in the bhava of parakiya-rasa. Furthermore, in order to eliminate any charge of impropriety raised by mundane moralists regarding Krishna's activities while enacting the parakiya-rasa pastimes, it is further explained by Shrila Jiva Goswami in his celebrated book Gopala-champu, that under the influence of the allpowerful yogamaya potency, only the shadow forms of the gopis had been married in their youth-hood; therefore the real forms of the gopis, including Shrimati Radharani, remained unmarried and thus any complaint of immorality raised by the materialist is thereby completely nullified. Another vital point that must be considered is that these pastimes of conjugal love were enacted by Krishna and the gopis from the age of seven till ten and thus any mundane concept of sexual promiscuity is redundant as boys and girls of that age are not sexually active. Thus it must be concluded that the conjugal-lila of Krishna and the gopis is a completely pure and transcendental display of prema-rasa or pure love of God, and meant to attract the fallen conditioned souls to realize the superlative feature of pure spiritual existence that all jivas are eligible to take part.

How To Get There: Yavat is 3km east of Nandagram (See map no.27E & 28).

## Places of Interest at Yavata

## 1 Jatila ki Haveli (Jatila's House)

This is the place on a small hillock where the ancestral home of Jatila was situated and where, after marriage, Radharani lived with Her supposed husband Abhimanyu, his mother Jatila and his sister Kutila. The word ‘haveli' means a 'large residence' with many rooms where many generations of the same family live together. This haveli is now a temple where one can see the Deities of Radha and Krishna known as Shri Shri Radha-Kanta. In another shrine to the left of the Deity room one can see the Deities of Jatila, Kutila, and Abhimanyu and on the roof there is a shrine known as Shringara-sthala which is dedicated the Krishna's pastimes of combing Radha's hair and decorating Her with cosmetics and jewelry. In the courtyard of the temple is a tree which local people call a moti-per or pearl-tree. It is said that when Krishna planted pearls in His garden near Moti-kunda at Nandagrama, it was this particular variety of tree that grew there and became covered with pearls instead of fruits.

How To Get There: This place is situated on a hill in the center of the village and is visible from many miles away (See map no. 23).

## Pastime Places Near Jatila Ki Haveli no Longer Visible

## 1a Beriya

The name Beriya refers to a ber tree, also spelt as baer and known in English as 'jujube' and it produces a small sweet yellow-colored fruit commonly called ber fruit, which is very popular with children all over India. This celebrated tree was the place where a very wonderful pastime took place. Formerly located in the courtyard of Jatila's house was a large ber tree where Krishna was once forced to hide the entire night during a failed attempt to meet Radharani. Once, Krishna came to the courtyard of Jatila's house late at night in the hope of meeting Radharani. Sitting on a branch of the ber tree, Krishna began signaling to Radha by imitating the sound of a cuckoo. Krishna then climbed down from the ber tree and was very stealthily moving towards the door when Jatila, who was only half asleep, on hearing some slight sound, suddenly called out, “Who's there? Who's there?” This sent Krishna scurrying back to the ber tree to hide. Each time Krishna tried to sneak past the half asleep Jatila, she would cry out, “Who's there?” and Krishna would have to immediately scurry back once again, and hide in the ber tree. This sequence of events went on a number of times and by dawn Krishna was forced to return home to Nandagrama without being able to meet Radharani.

The Padyavali of Shrila Rupa Goswami says, "When Krishna arrived in Radha's courtyard for Their rendezvous, His tinkling ornaments sounded as the cooing of cuckoos and other birds. He suddenly heard the door open, and He also heard the continual jingling sounds of conch-shell bracelets. When He heard the arrogant Jatila call out, 'Who's there? Who's there?' He became pained at heart. He spent that entire night hiding in a tree in a corner of the courtyard.”

## 1b Vatsakhora (Kidaka)

The word 'vatsa' means a 'calf', and ‘khora' means 'holy place'. Just behind Jatila's house was her goshala (dairy) where one day Jatila was expertly deceived by Krishna's friend Subala. On one occasion Radharani was feeling very angry at Krishna and being overcome with mana or lover's pique, She stayed at home, which caused great distress to Krishna. In order to help Krishna meet with Radharani, Subala came to Yavata on the pretext of searching for his lost calf. Subal enquired from the ever-watchful Jatila if she had seen his calf. Jatila replied that she had not seen the any calf. Regardless, Subala asked to search Jatila's goshala just in case his calf may have wondered inside along with Jatila's cows. On entering the goshala, instead of searching for the calf, Subala passed right through to the other side and arrived beneath Radharani's balcony. After calling Radharani, Subala explained about Krishna's great distress and lamentation at Her absence. Feeling very sorry to hear about Krishna's condition, Radharani immediately gave up Her anger and agreed to meet with Krishna. Subala then gave his own clothing to Radharani so She could disguise Herself as him and thereby sneak out of the house to meet Krishna.

After dressing-up in Subala's clothing and wearing Subal's trademark turban, Radharani made Her way back through the goshala. She then picked up a tiny calf and held it in front of Her in order to hide Her breasts and very stealthily made Her way out of the goshala and along the path to the place where Krishna was waiting. Seeing who she thought was Subala leaving the goshala, Jatila asked if he had found his lost calf. Radharani answered in a voice perfectly imitating Subala's own voice saying, “Yes, I have found my lost calf”, while thanking Jatila for her help. On arriving at the meeting place, Krishna could not recognize Radharani who was very expertly disguised as Subala. Krishna began lamenting before Subala about the absence of His beloved Radha, while thoroughly condemning Himself for having caused Her to become angry with Him and thus stay at home. Unable to tolerate the heart-wrenching scene any longer, Radharani immediately placed Her arms around Krishna's neck and embraced Him. Suddenly feeling the soft embrace of Radharani's arms and simultaneously smelling the exotic fragrance of Her transcendental body, Krishna immediately knew who it was and became filled with ecstatic love as He was reunited once again with His beloved Radharani.

## 1c Kutila-dushana-sthana

The word 'dushana' means to 'criticize' or 'find fault' and this is the place (sthana) where Jatila's daughter Kutila, Abhimanyu's antagonistic sister, tried to find fault with Radharani. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “Kutila takes great pleasure finding faults with Radha's behavior.” One day Kutila suddenly found Radha and Krishna secretly meeting each other in a room at this place and quickly locked the door from outside while shouting aloud that she had caught Radharani in a compromising position with Her secret lover. Due to the loud noise created by Kutila, everyone came running, including Jatila and Abhimanyu. When everyone had gathered around, Kutila triumphantly unlocked the door, but to everyone's surprise, all they saw was Radharani very peacefully engaged in worshiping a Deity of goddess Kali. Everybody suddenly turned on Kutila and condemned her for falsely criticizing Radharani. The bewildered Kutila was thus exposed and made to look like an envious fool. What Kutila and the others didn't know was that Krishna had very expertly disguised Himself as the Deity of goddess Kali.

## 1d Padmavati Vivaha Sthali

This is the place where Radharani and the gopis, in order to enjoy some fun, performed the wedding ceremony (vivaha) between Krishna and Chandravali's best friend Padma. On a signal from Radharani, the gopis began decorating Padma with flowers, mahendi, and various other paraphernalia just like a bride. After being decorated in this way, Padma, completely unaware of what was going on, was escorted by the gopis and seated next to Krishna on a throne. After tying the corner of Padma's sari to Krishna's dhoti, the gopis began showering flower petals and singing traditional wedding songs, which caused great embarrassment to Padma who tried to hide her face, although internally she was feeling completely ecstatic.

## 1e Panihari-kunda

The word 'panihari' means a place from where 'water is taken' and this is one of the kundas where the gopis used to come to fetch drinking water.

## 1f Pibana-kunda

The word 'piban' (pivana) means 'to drink' and this is the place surrounded by kadamba trees where, after being encouraged by the gopis, Krishna became intoxicated after He drank the nectar from Radha's lips. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, "At Pibana-kunda, within the forest of kadamba trees, Radha and Krishna play in the company of Their sakhis. Taking a hint from the sakhis, the eager Krishna becomes intoxicated by drinking the nectar of Radha's lips.”

## 1g Mukta-kunda

On the banks of this kunda, the sakhis would decorate Radharani with various ornaments made from pearls (mukta).

## 1h Krishna-kunda

This kunda is surrounded by banyana trees and was the site of many wonderful pastimes between Krishna and the gopis. This is also the place where Radha and Krishna used to enjoy swing pastimes known as jhulana-lila. The word ‘jhula' means a 'swing'.

## 1i Ladali-kunda

It is said that Lalita-sakhi would make arrangements for Radha and Krishna to secretly meet each other on the banks of this kunda. The word 'ladali' means a 'young girl' and refers to Radharani. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “Here is Ladili-kunda where Lalita secretly arranges the meeting of Rai and Kanu.” Both Rai and Kanu are pet names for Radha and Krishna.

## 1j Narada-kunda

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “O Shrinivasa, just see Narada-kunda. By taking bath here all one's desires are fulfilled.” It is said that this is the place where Durvasa Muni gave a special benediction to Radharani, that whatever she cooked would become nectar and whoever ate Her cooking would never get sick. Because of this benediction, Yasoda Mayi arranged to have Radharani cook for Krishna every day. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “At this place one muni benedicted Shrimati Radhika that whatever She cooked would become nectar.’ It is also said that Radharani would stand here in the morning with Her girlfriends and watch Her beloved Krishna head to the forests for grazing the cows while surrounded by His cowherd boyfriends.

## Visible Pastime Places at Yavat

## 2 Kishori Vata (Yavaka Vata)

This is the place where the famous banyana tree known as Yavaka Vata once stood. It is known locally as Kishori Vata and although the original banyan tree has disappeared, one can still see Kishori-kunda. There is also a Rasa-mandala that marks the spot where rasa-lila was performed. Kishori Vata is where Krishna decorated Radharani's lotus-feet with yavaka (red lac). There is a temple here where one can see the Deities of Krishna-Kishori. Radharani is sometimes called Kishori and this name refers to the period in Radha's life starting from the age of seven, referred to as Her kaishori-lila, when Radha performed innumerable amorous pastimes with Krishna during Her youth.

How To Get There: (See map no. 28).

## 3 Kishori-kunda

This kunda was one of the places where Radharani enjoyed pastimes with Her sakhis. It is said that Krishna would also enjoy water sports known as jal-krida pastimes with Radharani and the gopis in this kunda. Situated on the bank of the kunda is the Shri Kishoriji Mandira and nearby is Chira-kunda, where there is a Jhulan-sthali commemorating Radha and Krishna's swing pastimes that took place here.

How To Get There: (See Map no.28).

## 4 Rasa-mandala

This rasa-mandala platform on the banks of Kishori-kunda was established by Shrila Narayana Bhatta to commemorate the rasa-lila pastimes that took place at Yavata between Radha and Krishna.

How To Get There: (See Map no.28).

## 5 Parala-kunda (Piyala-kunda)

This kunda is also known as Parala-ganga and it is said that the water of the Ganges River appeared here just for the satisfaction of Radharani. There is an ancient parijata tree on the bank of this kunda which is said to have been planted by Radharani, who made garlands from its flowers which She offered to Krishna. There is still a tree at this same place which is said to flower once in a year in the month of Vaishakha (April/May).

How To Get There: (See Map no.28).

## 6 Charana-Kunda (Charana-ganga)

It is said that once Radharani was returning to Yavata from enjoying pastimes with Krishna in the nearby forest of Kokilavana, when She suddenly noticed Her feet were covered with mud from the forest floor. Radharani became anxious that Her mother-in-law Jatila would see the mud on Her feet and understand She had been loitering in Kokilavana with Krishna. At that moment Krishna suddenly manifested the Ganges River at this place by pressing His foot into the ground. Radharani could then wash the mud from Her lotus feet in the newly-formed kunda before returning home.

How To Get There: (See Map no.28).

## 7 Radhika-ka-gamana-patha

The word 'gamana-patha' means 'pathway' which was used by Radharani when She went to Surya-kunda each morning to worship the sun-god Suryadeva. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “Radha goes on this path to worship Suryadeva and She waits in this forest of kadamba trees to catch a glimpse of Her beloved Krishna. As Krishna approaches He catches hold of Her cloth, and in this way They both enjoy great fun”. The daily pastimes of Radharani performing puja at the sun-god's temple at Surya-kunda, as well as Her pastimes at Radha-kunda, form part of the ashta-kaliya-lila, or the eight-fold daily activities of the 'divine lovers' Radha and Krishna.

There is another path that leads from Yavata to Nandagrama that passes through Nanda Maharaja's garden. Radharani would use this path every day when She went to Nandagrama to cook Krishna's breakfast. Because She was such a wonderful cook, Mother Yashoda insisted that Radharani should always cook for Krishna. The Krishna-bhavanamrita says, “As She went out of the door and walked through Yavata village, Shri Radhika turned the narrow paths into streets of gold and jewels with the reflection of Her effulgent form, clothes and ornaments. The sweet fragrance of Her divine body pervaded all the directions. Out of shyness and to avoid the gaze of others on the path, She lowered Her eyes and covered Her lotus-like face with Her veil while keeping to one side of the path.”

How To Get There: (See Map no.28).

End of places of interest at Yavat

End of Chapter Six

## Chapter Seven: Kokilavana to Nanda Ghata

## 50 Kokilavana

This isolated and untouched verdant forest is still much the same although somewhat reduced in size. The forest abounds with many varieties of birds including the cuckoo (kokila) and many other forms of wildlife like deer and antelope. The Vraja-bhakti-vilasa says that Kokilvana is one of the sub-forests, or upavanas of Vrindavana, although in some Puranas it is mentioned to be one of the twelve dwadasha-vanas instead of Kadiravana, which is located a few miles to the south. Kokilavana is one of the forests where Krishna performed pastimes with Radharani and the gopis including the celebrated rasa-dance. The forest takes its name from the 'kokila' bird, which refers to the black colored Indian cuckoo also known as koel. This particular cuckoo has a loud shrieking call, ‘kuhoo, kuhoo, kuhoo', repeated in crescendo four or five times especially during the summer, sometimes in the early morning, but generally in late afternoon and evening. One day Krishna came to this forest in order to meet Radharani and the gopis, but due to the ever-watchful eye of Jatila, Radharani and the gopis could not leave the house. Understanding the situation, Krishna began to call the gopis by imitating the melodious song of the kokila bird, which inspired all the other kokila birds in the forest to start singing, thus creating a tumultuous sound that could be heard for miles and especially in the nearby village of Yavata.

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “To the west of Yavat is a forest where one may hear hundreds of thousands of kokilas sing. One day Krishna entered this forest and happily made a sound just like a kokila bird. In response, all the birds began singing so loudly that the sound was heard in Yavat. Hearing the sound of the kokilas, Jatila told Vishakha that she had never heard such songs from the kokilas. Vishakha replied that if Jatila would give them permission, the gopis would go to see the kokilas in the forest. Jatila then told them to go and listen to the birds and thus Radharani with Her girlfriends entered the forest. In unlimited happiness they came here and thus Radha was able to meet Krishna, who was engaged in making sounds of the kokila bird. For this reason this forest is known as Kokilavana.”

In the forest of Kokilavana one can see the rasa-mandala platform established by Shrila Narayana Bhatta to commemorate Krishna's rasa-lila pastimes in this forest and also Ratna-kunda, where it is said the gopis obtained many kinds of precious gemstones which they used in decorating Radharani. The word 'ratna' means ‘gemstones'. There are also two famous temples here: the Radha Kokila-Bihari Mandira dedicated to Radha and Krishna's pastimes at Kokilavana and the Shanideva Mandira, where large crowds gather on Saturdays, the day on which Hindus worship the demigod Shanideva, the predominating Deity of the planet Saturn. Top How To Get There: This forest is on the road from Nandagoan to Kosi and is 1.5km west of Yavat, and 5km north of Nandagoan (See map no.28A & 29).

## The Story of Kokilavana’s Shanideva Temple

It is mentioned in the Garga Samhita, that when all the demigods visited Nanda Maharaja's house to have darshana of baby Krishna, all them took darshana except Shanideva, because when Shanideva tried to enter the room to take darshana, mother Yashoda stopped him at the door saying, “You cannot see my baby because your very name fills everyone with fear and if my baby sees you, he may well be frightened.” Hearing these words, Shanideva felt very disappointed and decided to enter the nearby Kokilavana forest in order to perform penance in the hope that one day he might get the mercy of the Lord and achieve His darshana. After a sometime, Lord Krishna appeared before Shanideva and said, “What is the problem? Why are you performing penance in this forest alone?” Shanideva replied, “O Lord! Please enlighten me, when I am sincerely engaged in my duty to punish people according to their deeds (karma), why do people think that I am malignant and cruel? Why do people think that I create obstacles causing people to suffer? Why do they avoid even my shadow? When all the demigods had your darshana, I was denied that opportunity.” Hearing the words of Shanideva, Lord Krishna advised him to stay at Kokilavan and granted him the benediction that whoever comes to visit his shrine and offer prayers, would be freed from all worries and afflictions. Thus, Lord Krishna gave Shanideva his darshana and also made him famous as very few demigods have shrines in the holy land of Vraja.

## 51 Bada Baithana (Bathain Kalan)

There are two villages located very close to each another, the first one is called Bathain Kalan, also known as Bada Bathain (Big Bathain), while the second village is half a kilometer to the north and called Bathain Kurd, also known as Chota Bathain (Small Bathain). The name of both villages is derived from the word 'baithna' which means 'to sit down'. It is said that one day while herding the cows at this place, Krishna saw the gopis in the distance and asked Balarama to sit down (baithna) at this place and wait for Him while He went to meet Radharani. It is also said that Nanda Maharaja and his minister Upananda, would hold some of their important meetings at this village and the place where they took place was called the baithaka or sitting place. In the Bhakti-ratnakara it is said, “See this village named Baithana. When the cowherd men had a conference, everyone came to this place and sat. Because they all sat here, this place is known as Baithana.” The Bhakti-ratnakara also says that Shrila Sanatana Goswami often came to this village and spent time here performing bhajana, much to the satisfaction of the local Vrajavasis, who had great affection for Sanatana and held him in high esteem.

The location of Nanda Baba's baithaka is unknown but in the village one can visit the Dauji Mandira and Balabhadra-kunda, which is sometimes called Krishna-kunda, and is the place where the cowherd boys enjoyed water sports (jala-krida) with Krishna and Balarama. During the annual Holi-mela festivities, there is a huge celebration held on the banks of this kunda known as the Holanga-mela, where the local version of 'Lathamar-holi' is enacted. This is where the ladies of Bada Bathain enjoy abusing and then beating the men from Chota Bathain with long bamboo sticks known as lathis, while the men try to protect themselves with shields or broken off tree branches. The Holi-mela as well as Lathima-holi is celebrated in Varsana, Nandagrama and a number of other places around Vraja during the month of Phalgun (Feb/March).

How To Get There: This place is 3km north of Kokilavana (See map no.28A & 29).

## 52 Chota Bathain (Bathain Kurd)

Here in this village one can see Kuntala-kunda where Krishna sometimes came with the cowherd boys who used to comb and decorate Krishna's hair with forest flowers. The word 'kuntala' means 'lock of hair'. It is also said that the sakhis would also comb Radharani's hair and braid Her locks with forest flowers on the banks of this same kunda. In the village one can see a temple of Shakshi Gopala.

How To Get There: This place is (500mt) north of Bathain Kalan (See map no.28A & 29).

## 53 Charana Pahadi

This is where one can see the impression of Krishna's lotus feet indented in rock on top of the hill. There are three very famous Charana Pahadis in Vraja: Kamyavana, Nandagrama and here at Chota Bathain. The word 'charana' means Krishna's 'lotus feet' and 'pahadi' means a 'hill' or 'mountain'. Nearby is the kunda known as Charana-ganga where it is said that Krishna once washed His lotus feet. One day, Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends were herding cows near this village when they decided to climb to the top of the hill and observe the cows grazing in the pastures below.

Once on top of the hill, Krishna took out His flute and standing in His three-fold bending form known as tri-bhanga-rupa, began playing such an enchanting melody that it captivated the minds of the cowherd boys and all those who heard it. Being attracted by the sweet sound of the flute, the cows also arrived on top of the hill along with a number of forest animals including deer and antelopes; even some of local village people also came there attracted by the sweet sound of Krishna's flute. All those who had gathered on the hilltop remained motionless as if in a trance while listening to the ecstatic sounds emanating from Krishna's flute. The sound of the flute was so transcendentally mesmerizing that even the rocks on the hill started to melt in ecstasy. Because the rocks became softened due to the vibrations of the flute, the impressions of the feet of all those who had assembled there on the hilltop became impressed upon the rocks, including those of the cowherd boys, the cows, the various animals as well as those of the local Vrajavasis. Therefore, along with Krishna's lotus feet, one can also see the various impressions left by the cowherd boys, the Vrajavasis, the cows, deer, antelopes, birds and many other creatures. In the Bhakti-ratnakara it says, “At Charana Pahadi Krishna joyfully performed different pastimes. Once, Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends climbed this hill simply to see the beauty of the grazing cows. Dressed in attractive clothing, Krishna stood beneath a tree while playing His flute, standing in His threefold bending form. As soon as the sound of His flute was heard, people from all directions gathered near Him and stood motionless as they heard the sweet music. Within this earth is there any comparison to that heavenly music? Even the mountains melted at the sound of His flute.”

How To Get There: This place is 1km north of Baithana Khurd (See map no.28A & 29).

NOTE: If one is following the main Vraja Mandala Parikrama route one can visit Rasauli (X.120) on the way from Charana Pahadi to Dahgaon (see map 29).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 23

Including: \*Hulwana\* Kadauna\*Pakharapura\*Ledari\*Kamar\*Bicchor\*Tirwara\*Lalapur

## 111 Haroyala (Hulwana)

The name of the village is derived from the word 'hara' which means 'defeat' or 'loss' and at this place Krishna was defeated in a dice game by Radharani. Once Radharani told Lalita and the sakhis that Krishna was so strong that He easily defeated them in the games they playedbecause they were all based on bodily strength, therefore think of a game that is based on intelligence, by which Krishna can easily be defeated. Lalita then suggested that Radharani should challenge Krishna to a game of dice. The sakhis challenged Krishna to a dice game and accepting their challenge, Krishna sat down facing Radharani and started throwing the dice. However, Radharani very easily won the first few games. Feeling confident that His luck was changing, Krishna placed his flute as a wager, but Radharani once again won the game and took Krishna's flute as Her prize. Seeing Krishna repeatedly lose in the dice game, Madhumangala told Krishna, 'now the gopis have won your flute and next they will confiscate everything. I am not happy to see you lose like this, so just go back to your cow-herding activities'. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “Behold Krishna-kunda in the village of Haroyala where Radha and Krishna enjoyed Their divine pastimes. It was here that Radha defeated Krishna in a game of dice, causing great embarrassment to Krishna. Lalita then said to Radha 'You have easily defeated the master of your heart in this dice game, now let us see who will win in the battle of love’. Saying this, Lalita escorted Radha and Krishna to a nearby nikunja and then the sakhis secretly watched the amorous love-games of the 'divine couple’ from a hidden place. Seeing this divine loving relationship between Radha and Krishna, the sakhis felt themselves most fortunate.”

How To Get There: This village is 3km north-west of Bathain Kurd (See map no.29).

## 112 Kadona (Kadauna)

The name of the village is derived from the word 'dona' which means 'leaf cup’ and it was here that Krishna and His boyfriends ate yogurt from cups made of dried leaves.

How To Get There: This place is 1km south-west of Hulwana (See map no.29).

## 113 Pakharapura (Parkhapur)

In this village there is a very large lake created by Krishna. One day Krishna was playing here with His cowherd boyfriends when they all complained of feeling thirsty. Krishna took out His flute and began to play and within moments water started to come out from the ground, which very soon formed into a small lake and the cowherd boys could quench their thirst. The name of the village is believed to be derived from the word 'pokhara' or 'pukhura' which means a pond, or lake.

How To Get There: This place is 1.5km west of Kadauna (See map no.29).

## 114 Letari (Ledari)

It is said that one day the gopis were passing this place when they decided to sit down to rest for a while, thus the village received the name 'Letari’ which means to 'rest awhile’.

How To Get There: This place is 3.5km north of Pakhapura (See map no.29).

## 115 Kamari (Kamar)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “In Kamari-grama Krishna passionately waited for Radha.” At this place Krishna was filled with transcendental desire (kama) as He waited for His beloved Radharani to arrive for the secret meeting. The name of this village is derived from the word 'kama' which means 'lust’ or 'desire’, which are considered to be a transcendental and pure spiritual emotion when exhibited by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Shri Krishna.

How To Get There: This place is 3km north-east of Ledari & (5km) northwest of Baithana Khurd (See map no.29).

NOTE: From Kamari (Kamar) one may visit these isolated holy places including: Vichhedata-tirtha (Bicchor), Tiloyara (Tarabad), & Shringara Vata (Singar), before returning to Kamar.

## 116 Vichora/Vicchedata-Tirtha (Bicchor)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “In Vichora-grama Chandramukhi and Her friends met Krishna. After They sported, They returned to Their own homes feeling separation from each other. Therefore this village is called Vichora.” The name Vichora comes from the word 'viccheda' which means 'separation’ and at this place Krishna enjoyed intimate pastimes with Chandramukhi and Her girlfriends. When the time came for Them to return to Their homes, both Krishna and Chandramukhi began to feel intense separation (viccheda) from each other. The name Chandramukhi refers to the beautiful moon-faced Radharani. A verse from the Vraja-riti-cintamani provides another meaning to the word viccheda when it says, “There the gopis drank the nectar of the 'divine couples’ playful conversation and saw the 'divine couple’ maddened by Their mutual touch. The gopis came from all directions (viccheda ga) to see the 'divine couple’, and therefore this place became known as Vicchedata-tirtha.” According to this verse from Vraja-riti-chintamani, the words ‘viccheda ga' found in the Sanskrit verse means 'arriving from different directions’.

How To Get There: This place is 4km north-west of Kamar (See map no. 29 & 29A).

## 117 Tiloyara (Tirwara/Tirabada)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “In Tiloyara-grama Krishna would play without taking a moments rest.” At this place Krishna and the cowherd boys became so absorbed in playing games that they never cared to rest. Located at this place was a sweet-smelling grove of kadamba trees known as kadamba-khandi. This is where Radha and Krishna became so deeply absorbed in Their loving pastimes that not even a single moment was wasted. The word ‘tila' means 'a moment in time’ and because there was not even a moment’s interruption in Krishna’s ecstatic pastimes at this place, the village became known as Tiloyara.

How To Get There: This place is 5km west of Bichhor vai Nai (See map no.29A).

## 118 Shringara-Vata (Singar)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “See this Shringara-vata where Krishna decorated Radhika in different ways.” The word ‘shringara' means to ‘decorate’ or to 'dress with ornaments’ and the name of this village has been derived from the pastime of shringara-lila that took place here. There was formerly a very large forest here with many banyan trees, which in Sanskrit are called vata-vriksa. Beneath one of these vata-vriksa trees known as Shringara-vata, Krishna very expertly decorated Radharani with the sixteen types of ornaments. After Radharani was nicely decorated the gopis also decorated Krishna with sixteen types of ornaments, after which the gopis sat the 'divine lovers' on a swing and everyone enjoyed jhulana-lila pastimes.

How To Get There: This place is 3km north of Tiloyara and 5km north-west of Bichhor vai Jharokri (See map no.29A).

## 119 Lalapura

This place is mentioned in Bhakti-ratnakara as being a very beautiful spot where Krishna used to perform pastimes. It is also said that the great sage Durvasa Muni had a hermitage here; he was a partial expansion of Lord Shiva and spent a lot of time in Vrindavana Dhama. In the village one can see Durvasa-kunda as well as a small temple containing the Deity of Durvasa Muni.

How To Get There: This village is 2km north-east of Kamar (See map no.29).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 54 Dadi Grama / Daigoan (Dahgoan)

One day the gopis were carrying many large pots of yogurt to the nearby market and while passing this place they were suddenly set upon and looted of their yogurt pots by Krishna and the cowherd boys, who were out to have some fun in the name of tax collection and enjoy a free feast of yogurt at the expense of the gopis. The words 'dadi, 'dadhi', or 'dahi' means yogurt, and because this pastime of stealing the gopi's yogurt occurred at this place, the village achieved the name Dadi Grama. One can see in the village Dadhi-kunda, Sitala-kunda, and Madhusudana-kunda.

How To Get There: This village is 4km north of Baithana Khurd & Charana Pahadi (See map no.29).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 24

Including;\*Rasauli (Rashwan)

## 120 Rasauli (Rashwan/Raswan)

It is said that at this place Krishna performed rasa-lila with the gopis on the occasion of Saradiya-purnima that occurs in the Sarat season, corresponding to the lunar month of Ashvin (September to October).

How To Get There: This village is 2km south of Dahgoan (See map no.29).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 55 Kotaravana (Kotban/Kotwan)

This forest which is also called Kotvana is one of the upavanas or sub-forests mentioned in the Puranas. Krishna used to come here while herding the cows and enjoyed many childhood pastimes with His friends in this forest. The word 'kotara' means the bird species known as a 'woodpecker' and the name Kotaravana suggests that it was a forest where there were many woodpeckers (kotaras). Nearby are Sitala-kunda and Surya-kunda. Kotaravana is one of the most northerly points on the Vraja Mandala Parikrama route and from here the parikrama turns eastward towards Seshashayi and then south to Paigrama. During the medieval period, Kotban was located in a strategically important place as it straddled the Agra to Delhi road which was a major artery and lifeline in this region. Kotban is famous for its medieval sandstone fortress built by the king of Bharatpur that is located in the center of the town and overlooks the Agra to Delhi road.

How To Get There: Kotban is 4km north of Charana Pahadi and 5km north of Kosi (See map no.29 & 30).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 25

Including: \*Karman\*Bhulwana\*Hodal\*Sondhad\*Banchari.

## 121 Karamana (Karman)

One day, Krishna came to this part of Vraja while herding His cows. The word 'karamana' implies that one's mind is 'completely absorbed' in a particular thought. Since the early morning, Krishna was completely absorbed in thinking about Radharani and suddenly due to intense feelings of separation from Her, He fainted and fell to the ground almost unconscious, thus this place became known as Karamana.

How To Get There: This place is 4km from Kotwan (See map no.29B).

## 122 Bhulavana/Chalana-Shila (Bulwana)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “In this place called Chalana-shila, Krishna sat down being unable to move out of a mood of love.” One day, Krishna came to this forest with His cowherd boyfriends for herding the cows. While the cowherd boys were engaged in playing various games, Krishna simply sat on a stone beneath a kadamba tree completely absorbed in thoughts of Radharani. Seeing Krishna in such a motionless condition, Subala came over and asked Krishna what was the problem, and what was it that He was so deeply absorbed in thinking about while sitting all alone in the middle of the forest. Krishna then explained that He was feeling such an intense separation from Radharani that He was unable to move and couldn't stop thinking about Her even for a moment. Krishna also said He was even forgetting where He was or what He was supposed to be doing. Subala then told Krishna, "Radharani is now far away in Varsana and we are here in this forest, so for now just try to forget about Her and come and play with us. I promise that when we return from herding the cows in the afternoon, I will arrange for You to meet with Your beloved Radha.” On hearing Subala's comforting words, Krishna became pacified and told Subala, "All right then, but remember your words and don't forget them.” Feeling happy to hear the words of Subala, Krishna then joined His friends in playing various games. Thus this forest became known as Bhulavana, because it was here that Subala spoke (bulana) such soothing words to Krishna. The stone on which Krishna sat became famous as the chalana-sila. The word 'chalana' means 'motionless'.

How To Get There: This place is 1.5km north of Kotban (See map no.29B).

## 123 Hodal

It is believed that the Pandavas came here and spent some time during their period of exile, before moving on to Kamyavana. There is a forest near here known as Pandava-vana and also a lake known as Pandava-kunda.

How To Get There: This place is situated on the Agra-Delhi road and 3km north of Bulwana & 8km north of Kotban (See map no.29B)

## 124 Sondha (Sondhad)

The name of this village is derived from the name of Krishna's uncle Sananda, the younger brother of Nanda Maharaja, who lived with his family in this village.

How To Get There: This place is 4km north of Hodal (See map no.29B).

## 125 Vanchari (Banchari)

In the Bhakti-ratnakara it is said that Krishna performed many wonderful pastimes at this place. Vanchari is one of the most northerly places in Vraja Mandala where Krishna performed transcendental pastimes. The word 'vanchari' can mean a 'forest dweller' or a person who spends a lot of his time in the forest. This name was given to Krishna by the gopis because He spends His whole day in the forest while herding the cows; even in the night Krishna could be found loitering in the forest groves of Vrindavana where He would be enjoying rasa-lila and other transcendental pastimes with the gopis of Vraja.

How To Get There: This place is 2km north-east of Soundhad & 4km north of Hodel (See map no.29B).

End of excursion (Return To Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 56 Seshashayi

This is the famous Deity of Seshashayi Vishnu in His four-armed form of Narayana lying down on the celestial serpent Sesha Naga and being served by Lakshmi Devi, the goddess of fortune, who is massaging the Lord's lotus feet. The Deity of Lord Seshashayi is known locally by the name of Podhanatha. There is a beautiful kunda here located next to the temple known as Kshirasagara-kunda or sometimes as Kshira Samudra, which was created from Lord Krishna's mind. The word 'kshira', pronounced as 'shira', means 'milk', and the word 'sagara', as well as 'samudra', means 'ocean'. The name Seshashayi refers to the pastime where Lord Vishnu lays down to rest (shayi) on Sesha, the serpent expansion of Lord Balarama, whose soft white underbelly provides a very comfortable bedstead for the Lord to relax and enjoy His pastime of yoga-nidra, or mystic slumber. This holy tirtha has always been known by the name Seshashayi even in ancient times. According to the Adi-Varaha Purana, Seshashayi is mentioned to be one of the upavanas, or sub-forests of Vraja Mandala. Nearby to the Kshirasagara-kunda is a kadamba-khandi or grove of kadamba trees and a jhulana-sthali which commemorates the swing pastimes enjoyed at this place by Krishna and the gopis.

There are a number of versions regarding Krishna's pastimes here at Seshashayi, but the most widely accepted one mentioned in the Vraja-riti-chintamani is as follows: One day, Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends were herding their cows in this forest when they met with Radharani and the gopis who were attending a nearby recitation of the Vedic scriptures by brahmanas where Seshashayi Vishnu was being glorified. Hearing the recitation, Radharani had a sudden desire to see this particular pastime and began discussing with the other gopis the greatness of Seshashayi Bhagavana, when suddenly Krishna began boasting that He Himself was none-different from Seshashayi Bhagavana. The gopis, who were quite accustomed to hearing Krishna's boasting words, started laughing and told Him that He should either prove that he was Seshashayi or simply stop His idle boasting.

At that moment Krishna manifested from His mind a large kunda that became known as Kshirasagara or the 'Ocean of Milk'. He then manifested on the surface of the kunda the form Sesha Naga, the celestial serpent. Krishna then entered the kunda and lay down on the white couch-like underbelly of Sesha Naga in the transcendental mood (bhava) of Lord Seshashayi Vishnu. On seeing Krishna's sudden transformation as Seshashayi Vishnu, Radharani was overcome by ecstatic feelings and She immediately entered the kunda and after sitting on the couch-like body of Sesha, began massaging Krishna's lotus feet while absorbed in the mood (bhava) of Lakshmi Devi, the Goddess of Fortune. When the gopis saw this incredible pastime taking place before their eyes, they were completely amazed and became stunned due to the incessant flow of ecstatic emotions.

In the Vraja-riti-chintamani it says, “There Lord Krishna manifested the milk ocean and expanded Himself as Ananta Sesha, transformed Himself into Kshiradakashayi Vishnu, and then sat down on the body of Ananta. Shri Radha then became the beautiful Lakshmi Devi, who with humbly bowed head began to massage Lord Vishnu’s lotus feet. This sight greatly delighted Radha’s on-looking gop/-friends”.

This temple of Seshashayi Vishnu was visited by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu during His Vraja Mandala parikrama. When Lord Chaitanya saw the beauty of the Deity, He could not contain Himself and became overwhelmed with ecstatic love. While looking at Lakshmiji massaging the feet of Vishnu, He began to recite a verse from Shrimad-Bhagavatam, “O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing that your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in you. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety that your tender lotus feet might be wounded by pebbles as you roam about the forest path.”

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, "Shri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra came here for darshana of Seshashayi. Seeing the beauty of Seshashayi, His ecstasy increased and in that state of love He became overwhelmed. Those fortunate persons who saw the effulgence of the Lord also became maddened in ecstasy and tears flowed from their eyes. They concluded that He could not be an ordinary human being, but must be Seshashayi Bhagavan Himself in the dress of a sannyas/. While speaking, they looked continually at the moonlike face of Chaitanya.”

Local brahmanas say that Vajranabha Maharaja established the Deity of Seshashayi Vishnu, however, there are no historical records that substantiate the claim. Some commentators have said that this Deity of Seshashayi was discovered by Shrila Narayana Bhatta, but the Deity of Seshashayi Vishnu was seen by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu during His parikrama of Vraja in 1515, and therefore the Deity was present long before Shrila Narayana Bhatta arrived in Vrindavana Dhama in 1545, therefore the Deity was definitely not discovered by him.

How To Get There: This place is 5km east of Kotban (See map no.30 & 31).

## 56A Nandanavana

It is said that this beautiful forest was named after Nanda Maharaja who often came here to perform bhajana.

How To Get There: This place is 1.5km south of Seshashayi (See map no.30 & 31).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 26

Including: \*Vasosi\*Khanbi\*Hasanpur\*Maholi\*Kharot\*Khararo\*Banchauli\*Phalain.

## Holy Places Located to The North &amp; South of Seshashayi

## 126 Vasosi (Basosi/Banswa)

The name of this village is derived from the word 'vasa' which means ‘fragrance’. In the Bhakti-ratnakara it is said, “Here is Vasosi Grama, which is perfumed by the scent from Krishna’s body. What to speak of maddening the bumblebees, the composure of the entire world is destroyed by that scent. It was here that Radha and Krishna played hol/ with Their dear friends.”

How To Get There: This place is 1.5km north of Seshashayi (See map no.30).

## 127 Khani-Grama / Khambahara (Khandi)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “Then there was Khani-grama in Khambahara, where Krishna and Balarama grazed Their cattle. Khani-grama is on one boundary of Vraja.” The name of this village is derived from the word 'khamba' which means a 'stone pillar'. This particular pillar is said to have been established here on top of a hill by King Vajranabha to mark the northern boundary of Vraja. In this regard the boundary in question marks the inner-core area of Vraja where all the lila-sthana's or pastime places including the twelve sacred forests (dwadasa-vana) are located.

How To Get There: This place is 9km north of Basosi (See map no.30).

## 128 Hasanpura

One day, Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends were herding their cows at this place. All the cowherd boys gathered around Krishna and asked Him how it was possible that even as a baby, He could perform such heroic activities and kill so many powerful demons like Putana, Trinavarta, and Shakatasura. Krishna immediately began to smile at the enquiry made by His friends and told them that these were just ordinary activities for Him. He then told the cowherd boys that it was very difficult to understand how He could exhibit such power while still a baby, and that it was an aspect of His yogamaya mystic potency. The word 'hasya' or 'hasya-rasa' means to 'smile' or to 'joke' and because it was here at this place where Krishna was smiling at the enquiry of His friends, this village became known as Hasanapura.

According to some Vaishnava babajis performing the Vraja Mandala Borderline-Parikrama, just south of Hasanpur on the parikrama path is a village named Mahali (Maholi) that is well known in the area as the residence of many Krishna-bhaktas, who all have Vaishnava tilak and wear tulasi neckbeads. It is said that there is no distinction of caste or creed everyone in the village chants the holy names of the Lord.

How To Get There: This village is 6km east of Khanbi (See map no.30).

## 129 Kharot (Kharot/Kharaut)

This village is located in the region where Krishna and Balarama were engaged in Their daily activities of go-charana-lila or the pastime of herding Their cows.

How To Get There: This place is 15km south of Hasanpur on the Hasanpur-Hodal road (See map no.30 & 31).

## 130 Kharero (Kharero/Khayero)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “This is where Balarama enquired about the well-being of His friends, the cowherd boys.” When Lord Balarama came from Dwaraka He travelled to various places in Vraja to meet His cowherd boyfriends. The word 'khaira' means 'news' and because Balarama wanted to get 'news' or 'information' about His friends at this place, the village became known as Kharero.

How To Get There: This village is 5km southeast of Seshashayi (See map no.31).

## 131 Banachauli (Barchawali)

It is said that Krishna performed rasa-lila pastimes at this place with the gopis.

How To Get There: This place is 2.5km north-east of Kharero (See map no.31)

## 132 Phalain

At this place the gopis seated the 'divine couple' Radha and Krishna on a throne and began singing enchanting love songs and dancing to the rhythmical sounds of their musical instruments. While the gopis were ecstatically dancing they began throwing red colored gulal on the bodies of Radha and Krishna. In the village there is a kunda called Shri-Kunda.

How To Get There: This place is 4 km south of Hasanpur (See map no.31).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 57 Paya Grama (Paigoan)

In the Bhakti-ratnakara it is said, “In Paya-grama, Krishna drank paya with His friends.” The name of the village is derived from the word ’paya' or 'payai' which refers to milk. The village achieved its name because one day Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends were feeling hungry and as mother Yashoda had not arrived with lunch, Krishna and his sakhas came to this place where they were offered paya by the ladies of the village. There is a kunda in the village called Paya-sarovara.

How To Get There: This place is 4km south-east of Phalain & and 4km west of Shergarh (See map no.31 & 31A).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 27

Including: \*Ujani.

## 133 UJANI (Ujhani Kadar/Ujhiani)

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “In Ujani, the Yamuna changed her course and flowed upstream while listening to the sweet music of Krishna's flute.” This village is situated near the banks of the River Yamuna. The word 'ujani' means ‘opposite direction’ and refers to the day when, after hearing the transcendental sound of Krishna’s flute, the Yamuna River became temporarily stunned due to ecstasy and started to flow in the opposite direction with her current suddenly flowing upstream instead of downstream.

How To Get There: This village is 5km north of Shergarh (See map no.31A).

End of excursion (Return To Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 58 Khelanvana (Shergarh)

Situated on the banks of the River Yamuna is the famous forest known as Khelanvana where Krishna and Balarama spent many long hours playing with Their friends. This forest is mentioned in the Vraja-bhakti-vilasa as being one of the prativanas (sub forests) of Vrindavana Dhama. The name ‘Khelanvana’ means ‘the playground forest’. Krishna and Balarama would be so absorbed in playing games in this forest that They would forget to take Their lunch and mother Yashoda would have to personally call Them and on some occasions bring Their lunch to the forest. The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “In Khelanvana, now called Khela-tirtha, Krishna and Balarama played continually, forgetting even Their food until Their mothers came to feed Them.”

This place is also known as Kela-tirtha which means the sacred place (tirtha) where children play games (kela). This forest is also referred to as 'Kridavana', which means a 'forest where children engage in sporting activities'. These childhood pastimes at Khelanvana began when Krishna moved from Gokula to Shakatikara and started to graze His calves in this area which is known as 'Nanda's Vraja'. Later, when He moved to Nandagrama, Krishna used to meet the gopis here and this is one of the forests where rasa-lila pastimes took place. The name of this town however changed when the Sultan of Delhi, Sher Shah Suri, who had conquered a large portion of Northern India, decided to build a fort here and thus changed the name of the town to Shergarh. The ruins of the Sultan's fort can still be seen but the large forest of Khelanavana is no longer visible.

How To Get There: This place is 7km east of Paigram & 12km east of Chhata (See map no. 31A & 32).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 28

Including: \*Chhinparai\*Pahadi\*Basau\*Bajna\*Tilakgadhi\*Marava\*Venuya.

NOTE: There are six holy places on the eastern bank of the Yamuna and the easiest way to reach them is to cross the river at Shergarh (Khelanvana). This area was not visited during the parikrama of Lord Chaitanya, or the parikrama led by Raghava Pandita, however these holy places in the northern sector east of the Yamuna were mentioned by Raghava Pandita after he crossed the Yamuna at Nanda Ghata and reached the village of Sarkaroya on the eastern bank. Two of these holy places namely Marava and Bhajana are also visited by the Vraja Mandala Borderline-Parikrama and Marav also marks the northernmost lila-sthana on the eastern bank of the Yamuna.

## 134 Chhina Pahadi (Chhinparai)

It is said that Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends once looted milk from the gopis at this place while they were on their way to sell their products in a local market.

How To Get There: This place is 3km north of Shergarh (See map no.32).

## 135 Basau

It is said that after looting milk from the gopis at Chhina Pahadi, Krishna and His cowherd boyfriends came here and after sitting down on the banks of the Yamuna, they very happily drank all the milk.

How To Get There: This place is 1.5km west of Chhinnaparai (See map no.32).

## 136 Bajna

The name Bajna is derived from the word 'bhajana' which means 'to sing or play musical instruments'. It is said that one day, after having seated Radha and Krishna on a splendid flower bedecked throne, the cowherd boys began playing drums and various instruments while the gopis sang songs glorifying Radha and Krishna while many other gopis danced in a circle around the 'divine couple'. Bajna is located on the Vraja Mandala Borderline-Parikrama.

How To Get There: This place is 11km north of Chhinaparai & Basau (See map no.32).

## 137 Tilakgadhi / Manighadhi

This village became famous because all the local Vrajavasi village people wore Vaishnava tilak on their foreheads, which was due to the influence of a very great Vaishnava saint who once lived in the village. This same saintly person was also known to possess a valuable jewel (mani) which he threw into the Yamuna River and because of this the nearby village of Manighadhi achieved its name.

How To Get There: This place is 7km north-west of Nauhjhil & 9km west of Bajna (See map no.32).

## 138 Marava

This village marks the northern border of Vraja on the eastern bank of the Yamuna River and those pilgrims performing the Vraja Mandala Borderline-Parikrama visit this place. The samadhi of the celebrated sage Markandeya Rsi can be found here on a small hill at the place where he underwent austerities and the name Marava is derived from the name of Markandeya.

How To Get There: This place is 5km north of Tilakgadhi & 14 km north-west of Bajna (See map no.32).

## 139 Venuya

It is said that at this place on the bank of the Yamuna, Krishna stole the gopis minds after they heard the enchanting sound of His transcendental flute. Krishna's flute is also known as a venu and thus the village became known as Venuya because it was here that Krishna enchanted the gopis with His venu or flute.

How To Get There: This place is 6km south-west of Nohjhil (See map no.32).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 59 Rama Ghata (Ohava/Obe/Oba Bangar)

This is the celebrated place near the banks of the Yamuna where Lord Balarama once dragged the River Yamuna with His celebrated plough weapon known as haladhar. This happened during the time when Lord Balarama was performing rasa-lila pastimes with His cowherd girlfriends at this place. One can see the temple of Dauji (Balarama) known as Khencha-Dauji Mandira. The word 'khencha' means 'to drag' or 'to pull' and refers to Lord Balarama having dragged Yamunaji with His plough at this place, and the word 'dauji' means 'Krishna's elder brother'. Rama Ghata is a prominent pastime place of Lord Balarama and it is also mentioned in Vraja-bhakti-vilasa as one of the upavanas (sub-forests) of Vrindavana Dhama. It is said that a sakha, or cowherd boyfriend of Lord Balarama took birth as an ashvata-vriksha (peepal tree) here at Rama Ghata and that ancient tree can still be seen even today.

After Krishna and Balarama's departure from Vrindavana, the Vrajavasis were always feeling the pangs of acute separation and on Krishna's advice, Balarama came from Dwaraka to spend time with the Vrajavasis and help soothe their feelings. On His arrival at Nandagrama, Balarama met everyone including mother Yashoda, Nanda Maharaja, the gopis and the gopas, and spent many long hours talking with them and was able to somewhat pacify them with His soothing words of heartfelt encouragement.

In the Bhakti-ratnakara it says, “O Shrinivasa, this is Rama Ghata. Balarama, the son of Rohini, performed His rasa-lila here. Knowing that He would perform His rasa-lila with His dear lovers, Balarama happily came to this place. This pleasant spot, situated near the Yamuna River, was always filled with scented air. The flowers of the gardens were in full bloom and the sky was bright from the full moon. The humming of bumblebees and the sweet singing of various birds surcharged the atmosphere. Millions of male and female peacocks danced and many deer played in the garden. As Balarama relaxed beneath a tree, the gods in heaven sang the glories of Rohini-nandana whose beauty and posture fascinate the world.”

“O Shrinivasa, who can keep his composure seeing the splendor of Baladeva? It was here that Rama (Baladeva) sat on a jeweled throne in a festive dress. The beauty of Baladeva conquers that of millions of Kamadevas and every movement of His charms the munis and Indras. The glory of His body which brightens the three worlds can defeat the pride of a million moons. The silky black curly hair covering His head is decorated with a jewel-set crown and He wears a flower garland. His lips are as red as bimba fruit and His teeth sparkle like pearls. A garland of Vaijayanti dangles from His powerful neck.”

“All glories to the powerful hero, Rohini-nandana. The white conch, kunda flowers, camphor, and the silver-white mountain, all bow down to Balarama's bright white complexion. The wavy locks of His lustrous hair, curling around His forehead and His bright tilaka steals the young maidens' hearts. His lotus eyes are restless and His eyebrows dance like black bumblebees near His bright earrings. With a pointed nose that defeats the beauty of Garuda's beak and His face which conquers the splendor of the moon, it appears as though nectar pours from His body. His arms are decorated with bangles, and jeweled necklaces adorn His strong chest. His thin waist breaks the lion's pride. He is wearing an exquisite blue dress and His wellshaped knees are very pleasing to all who see Him. The reddish color of the soles of His feet defeats the sun and the brightness of His nails conquers the darkness.”

“I am unable to describe the beauty of Baladeva as there is no comparison to Him in this world. In this way the Puranas give Baladeva's descriptions which the fortunate must always see. In this place Rohini-nandana, Balarama, stood in a threefold bending form and blew joyfully on His horn, the sound of which moved the heart of Brahma and others. O Shrinivasa, with only one mouth how can I describe the beauty of Balai's pastimes? Here in this moon-lit Yamuna-upavana, Balarama engaged in pastimes surrounded by millions of gopis.”

During the period of Balarama’s two months stay in Vraja, many new gopis were lamenting before Him that they were far too young at the time to take part in His Vrindavana pastimes. There were also those girls who in their former lives had been the daughters of the Naga king who became gopis by the blessings of Lord Sesha Naga. In order to fulfill the desires of these various gopis to enjoy conjugal love, on the occasion of the full-moon night, Balarama invited them all to Rama Ghata and along with all His former girlfriends after drinking varuni nectar, a type of honey liquor, Lord Balarama engaged in the most ecstatic rasa-lila pastimes.
