## 199 Gopalaji Mandira (Brahmachari Mandira)

This large and ornate temple was built in the year 1860 by the king of Gwalior, Maharaja Jiyaji Scindia, on the order of his guru whose name was Giridharidas Brahmachari, thus the temple is also known as the Brahmachari Mandira.

How To Get There: (See map no.52).

## 200 Lala Babu Mandira (Krishna-Chandrama Mandira)

This beautiful and ornate temple was built in the year 1810 by the wealthy Bengali landowner from Calcutta named Krishna Chandra Sinha, who later became famous in Vrindavana as Lala Babu. One day while resting at home he heard the ominous words, 'it is time to wake-up', spoken to him by one of his family members. Lala Babu got a sudden jolt after hearing these prophetic words and believed it to be an omen and an important spiritual instruction. Having spent his whole life in the lap of maya surrounded by all the worldly attachments of family life, Lala Babu believed the ominous words to be a spiritual wake-up call and the Lord's special mercy upon him. Lala Babu decided to renounce all worldly matters and immediately left home for Vrindavana, where he lived the life of a renounced vairagi-baba. He utilized his immense wealth in building temples and securing various plots of land on which important Vaishnava tirthas stood. He also arranged for the construction of the sandstone ghatas around Radha-kunda.

How To Get There: (See map no.52

## 201 Jnana-gudari (Gyana Gudri)

Jnana-gudari is known these days as Gyana-gudri and is the name given to this sacred spot beneath an ancient banyan tree (vata-vriksha) where it is said that Krishna's dear most friend Uddhava, received the essence of Vedic knowledge (jnana-gudari) regarding the transcendental nature of Krishna's pastimes from Vidura. The word 'gudari' means 'to strain', or a 'straining cloth', used to extract juice from crushed fruit. Thus the name Jnana-gudari implies that the essence of Vedic knowledge (jnana) was extracted (gudari) by Vidura for the benefit of Uddhava. During that meeting, Uddhava reminded Vidura that he was the very last person that Krishna spoke with before the Lord's disappearance from the world. Uddhava mentioned this three times over, which caused Vidura to shed a torrent of tears as he remembered Krishna's special mercy upon him. Gyana-gudri was previously situated very near the banks of the River Yamuna before the river moved one kilometer eastward from its ancient course. It is said that when the Yamuna was in spate the flood waters would reach up to Gyana Gudri. It is said that Gyana Gudri also became famous because Prayag Tirtharaj once came to this place in the personified form of a black horse in order to bathe in the Yamuna River so that he could become free from all the accumulated sins left behind by the pilgrims who take bath in the Triveni-sangam at Prayag (Allahabad). After bathing in the Yamuna, Prayag Tirthraj, in the form of the black horse, turned completely white, having been freed from all the sins. Besides the ancient vata-vriksha (banyana tree) at Gnana Gudri, there is also an ancient well known as Gopa-kupa, which is one of Vrindavana's famous wells (kupa). Gopa-kupa, as the name suggests, was a well used by the gopas' as they passed along the cowherd boys trail on the bank of the Yamuna during their cow-herding pastimes.

How To Get There: (See map no.52).

## 202 Radha Vraja-mohana Mandira

The Deity of Vraja-Mohana was originally installed by Shrila Narottama Dasa Thakura during the famous Kheturi festival in Bengal, which was the first-ever Gaura Purnima celebration held to commemorate the appearance day of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. All the great Vaishnavas of the time attended the Kheturi festival, including Lord Nityananda's beloved consort Jahnava Mata and her son Balabhadra. During this festival five sets of Deities were installed by Narottama Dasa, while Narottama's dear most companion Srinivasa Acharya performed the abhisekha ceremony for these Deities. Vraja-Mohana is the only Deity installed at the Kheturi festival to have been brought to Vrindavana although there is the pratibhu-murti of Narottama's Gauranga Mahaprabhu presently being worshiped at the Radha Gokulananda Mandira.

How To Get There: (See map no.52).

## 203 Tekari Rani Mandira

The Tekari Rani Mandira is one of the finest examples of traditional North Indian temple archtecture. This magnificently ornate temple was built in the year 1871 by Rani Inderjit Kunver, the queen of Tekari, a small principality which was located in the State of Bihar in Eastern India.

How To Get There: (See map no.52).

## 204 Jagannatha Ghata (Jagannatha Mandira)

According to the legend surrounding Jagannatha Ghata, about two hundred years ago, a Ramanandi Vaishnava sadhu named Haridasa, who was an ardent devotee of Lord Krishna, used to perform his bhajana on the banks of the Yamuna near Vamsi Vata. It is said that one night Haridasa had a dream in which Lord Jagannatha appeared before him. The Lord informed Haridasa that He would be very happy to come to live on the banks of the Yamuna River in Vrindavana and accept the worship of Haridasa. Lord Jagannatha told Haridasa to immediately go to Puri in Orissa, as it was the time every twelve years, when the wooden body (Daru-Brahma) of the Deity was being changed for a new one. Lord Jagannatha told Haridasa that he should bring the old body of the Deity back to Vrindavana. On waking the next morning, Haridasa called all his disciples and associates together and revealed the details of the dream, after which, with a rousing kirtan they immediately left on foot for Puri.

On his arrival in Puri, Haridasa went to meet the head priest of the Jagannatha temple to request the old body of Lord Jagannatha. However, the head priest refused saying it was the age-old tradition of the temple to submerge the old body of the Deity in a sacred well within the temple compound. The head priest advised Haridasa to speak directly with the king of Puri, who was the senior most temple administrator. The king of Puri, after hearing the request made by Haridasa, also refused to grant permission for Haridasa to take the old body, as per the ancient customs of the Jagannatha temple, it would be placed in samadhi.

After both the head priest and King had refused the request of Haridasa, he went to the sea beach and decided to fast unto death as he had failed in his endeavor to obtain the old body of the Deity as instructed by the Lord in his dream. That night, the king had a dream in which Lord Jagannatha appeared in a very angry mood and demanding to know why the king had refused to follow the order given by the Lord Himself to his servant Haridasa. On waking the king immediately called for Haridasa and informed him of the dream. He then granted permission for Haridasa to take the old body of the Deity to Vrindavana. The king arranged for a horse-drawn chariot to carry the Deities of Jagannatha, Baladeva, and Subhadra, and accompanied by temple priests and a large contingent of soldiers, Haridasa brought the Deities to Vrindavana and installed Them on the bank of the Yamuna at the place which became known as Jagannatha Ghata. Some years later a temple was built at the ghata where the Deities still reside.

How To Get There: (See map no.52).

## 205 Mirror Mandira (Radha-nama Bank)

This unique temple is known as the Kanch Mandira and it is a popular place with Indian pilgrims visiting Vrindavana. The word ‘kanch' means 'glass mirror' and the walls of this temple are decorated with thousands of small mirrors. The temple was built by Maharaja Sawan Singh Juedeva, the king of Begawara in Madhya Pradesh. The Deities in this temple are Jugala-Kishore and there is also a Deity of baby Krishna lying in a jula (swinging cradle) at the front of the altar. In the courtyard of this temple is the Radha-nama Bank, where pilgrims are encouraged to write on a paper the holy names of Radha and Krishna as many times as possible. The paper or notebook is then deposited in the bank for the spiritual benefit of the writer. Writing the holy names of the Lord on paper or in books, is one of the methods undertaken by lay-persons who are not accustomed to chanting on beads.

How To Get There: (See map no.52).

## 206 Rangaji Mandir

The Rangaji Mandira is one of Vrindavana's largest temples built in the traditional South Indian style in 1851 by the family of the wealthy Mathura merchant Lakshmi Chand Seth. The Seths were originally Jains, but were converted to Vaishnava Dharma by one of the acharyas of the Ramanuja sampradaya. The temple has been constructed on a very grand style at a great expense. The sixty foot high Garuda-stambha at the entrance to the shrine is covered with pure gold plate. The temple is reminiscent of the original Rangaji temple at Trichy in Tamil Nadu and there are many artifacts in pure gold of Southern Indian origin that can be seen in the temple.

The presiding Deity in this temple is Seshashayi Vishnu, the form of Lord Vishnu reclining on the celestial serpent Sesha Naga. The temple is famous for the annual ten-day Brahmotsava celebration held from Chaitra Krishna-dvitiya (two days after Holi) and also a Ratha-yatra festival held on Chaitra Krishna-ashtami that attracts large crowds from the Vraja region. During the festival a pure sandalwood chariot carrying the main temple Deity is taken of Lord Ranganatha is taken in procession to the Rangaji Bagh Gardens. There is also a famous kunda at the rear of the temple known as Gajaraja-kunda where the pastime of Gajendra-mokshana, the liberation of Gajendra, the king of elephants, is celebrated during the month of Shravana (July-August)

How To Get There: (See map no.52 & 53).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 38 Brahma-kunda

It was here at Brahma-kunda that Shrila Rupa Goswami discovered the Deity of Vrinda Devi that was lying hidden on northern bank of the kunda, after the goddess herself appeared in a dream and informed him where she could be found. The Deity of Vrinda Devi, the presiding Deity of Vrindavana forest, is said to have been originally established by Vajranabha Maharaja. Some scholars have said that this sacred kunda was formed from the tears of Lord Brahma, who sat here for some time after he realized his mistake of having stolen Krishna's calves and cowherd boyfriends. In the Varaha Purana it says. “A person who fasts thru the night and bathes in beautiful Brahma-kunda, which is surrounded by many trees and vines, enjoys pastimes with the Gandharvas and Apsaras. Leaving one’s body here, he goes to my abode.”

In the Bhakti-ratnakara it says. “See this place Brahma-kunda which is very secluded and beautified by many creepers and plants. At this place, Vrinda Devi disclosed her mind and fulfilled the desires of Narada Muni.” With regard to this verse from Bhakti-ratnakara, some say it refers to Vrinda Devi advising Narada on how to achieve the form of a gopi in order for him to enter the rasa-mandala, after which he bathed in Brahma-kunda and obtained the form of a gopi. However according to most authorities, Narada bathed in Kusuma-sarovara to obtain the form of a gopi and this is also confirmed by Vishvanatha Chakravarti in Vraja-riti-chintamani. Some have proposed that Lord Shiva also bathed in Brahma-kunda in order to achieve the form of a gopi so that he could also enter the rasa-mandala to witness the rasa-dance, although the general opinion is that Lord Shiva bathed in Manasarovara to achieve the form of a gopi.

## 39 Radha Govinda Mandira

This is one of the famous 'Seven Goswami Temples' that was inspired by Shrila Rupa Goswami, who discovered the Deity of Lord Govinda buried in the ground at the site where the majestic temple of Govindaji now stands. The Deity of Govindaji was originally installed five thousand years earlier by Krishna's great grandson Vajranabha Maharaja, at the place known as the Govindaji yoga-pitha. After the discovery of the Deity, a small shrine was immediately built and the worship of the Deity began. There are no records of the actual date when the first seva-puja of the Deity was performed by Shrila Rupa Goswami, but it was definitely sometime before 1534, the year in which Lord Chaitanya disappeared, because after hearing about the discovery of the Govindaji Deity, Lord Chaitanya had personally sent some of the devotees from Puri to assist Rupa Goswami in serving the Deity. Rupa Goswami also discovered the Deity of Vrinda Devi at Brahma-kunda and she was installed in a separate shrine to the left of the main Deity room. This shrine stands directly above the actual hole within the ground where Govindaji was discovered by Rupa. This shrine which is below ground had its own temple tower and adjoins the southern side of the main temple, is the actual site of the Vrindavana Yoga-pitha.

When Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu directed Rupa Goswami to spend the rest of his life in Vrindavana, He asked him to fulfill four important tasks including: excavation of the lost holy places, write books on devotional service, establish the principles of Deity worship, and build temples, He also asked Rupa to specifically find the long-lost Deity of Govindaji, the presiding Deity of the northern petal of the lotus of Vraja Mandala. After arriving in Vrindavana and having searched for many days, Rupa could not find the location where the Deity of Govindaji was lying hidden. It is said that one day, after searching without success, feeling somewhat despondent, Rupa Goswami went to sit near the bank of the Yamuna, probably at nearby Pani Ghata, and was lamenting to himself saying, “Oh Chaitanya, Oh Chaitanya” Suddenly, a charming young cowherd boy came there and asked the cause of Rupa's dispair. After hearing about Rupa's search for Govindaji, the boy informed him that a cow was going every day to a nearby tila, or small hill, and was pouring milk from its udder into a hole in the ground. The cowherd boy asked Rupa to see what was in the hole. Realizing that this could be the clue that he had been looking for, Rupa accompanied the cowherd boy to the hill where the hole was located. On reaching the spot, Rupa peered into the hole in the earth and suddenly had the spiritual realization that this was the location where the Deity of Govindaji was buried. Rupa suddenly felt a rush of ecstatic symptoms throughout his being and momentarily fell unconscious. On regaining his senses, the cowherd boy had disappeared. Rupa concluded within his mind that the boy must have been Krishna Himself, disguised as a local cowherd boy, who had guided him to the spot where the Deity was buried. Rupa summoned the help of a few others and very carefully started digging into the hole. A few feet below the surface they suddenly saw the Deity of Govindaji. Loud cries of 'Jaya Govinda! Jaya Gopala!' rent the air as they slowly hauled the Deity out of the hole. After performing an abhishekha and instillation ceremony, the worship of the beautiful Deity of Lord Govindaji began once again after a lapse of almost five thousand years. On hearing about the wonderful discovery of the Deity of Govindaji, Lord Chaitanya sent some of His followers from Puri to help Rupa in the Deity worship, so that Rupa might continue with the important work of further excavation of Vrindavana's holy places and also writing books.

Some years after the discovery of Govindaji, in faraway Orissa, the son of Prataparudra Maharaja whose name was Purushottama Deva, had a dream one night in which a Deity being worshiped in the Jagannatha Temple as Lakshmi Devi, appeared before him and said, “I am not Lakshmi but Radharani, and I have been waiting for my beloved Govinda to again manifest in Vrindavana, so therefore please send Me to Vrindavana.” After receiving the dream, Purushottama consulted with the temple priests, temple authorities, and senior Vaishnavas, and after everyone agreed, the Deity of Lakshmi Devi was sent to Vrindavana. The Deity was then installed on the simhasana as Radharani and placed on the left-hand side of Lord Govinda. This was the first temple installation of a Deity of Radharani anywhere in the world. After this famous episode, gradually other Deities of Radharani were installed in other Goswami temples in Vrindavana and thus the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition of establishing temples with the Deities of both Radha and Krishna began. The exact date when the instillation of Radharani at the Govindaji Mandira took place is unknown, but it occurred sometime between 1534 and 1541, because after this date Purushottama Deva was assassinated by the army general Govinda Vidyadhara.

Previous to the time it was accepted that Radharani was automatically present along with Krishna, in Her un-manifested form as hladini-shakti, the internal pleasure potency of Krishna. This is because Radha and Krishna can never be separated and are eternally one and the same. It has also been said that Prataparudra's son Purushottama Deva, also sent another Deity of Radharani to be installed in the Madana-Mohana Mandira.

After the historic visit of Emperor Akbar to Vrindavana in 1570, the king of Jaipura and commander-in-chief of Akbar's army, Raja Man Singh, an ardent follower of the Goswamis and a disciple of Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami, requested permission from Akbar to construct the Govindaji Mandira and other Goswami temples in Vrindavana. Akbar gave his approval and also offered to provide high quality red sandstone from which the Govindaji Mandira was built. This rare sandstone had previously been reserved exclusively for Mughal palaces and forts. Although Rupa Goswami had by this time already entered samadhi, the construction began under the guidance of Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami. The temple construction was supervised by the king of Jaipura, Raja Man Singh, and all the best architects, engineers, and stone masons, were employed by the king in constructing this temple, which was recognized at that time as one of the greatest temples in India. This temple combined elements of Hindu, Christian, and Islamic architecture, and therefore, besides looking like a traditional Hindu temple, its unique design bears striking resemblance to both a mosque and a cathedral. The Govindaji Mandira, which opened in 1590, became the most impressive edifice that 'Hindu art' had ever produced in the whole of Northern India. The intricate carving of the sandstone and the series of balconies and archways that can be seen around the entire structure is unique. A separate shrine was also constructed at the actual site of the Govindaji Yoga-pitha where the Deities of Vrinda Devi and Yogamaya Devi were installed.

Raghava Pandita, Narottama and Shrinivasa Acarya also had darshana of Lord Govindaji some years before the construction of the Govindaji temple. The Bhakti-ratnakara says. “Then they all went to see Shri Govindadeva whose beauty and sweetness are described by the learned. After taking darshana of Shri Govinda, the three devotees became filled with ecstasy and their eyes and minds were fully satiated. On seeing the three devotees, Shri Krishna Dasa Pandita (Govindaji's pujari) became jubilant. He gave them garlands and prasada and inquired about their well-being. In ecstasy, Shri Raghava Pandita gradually explained everything about their darshana of the holy places of Vraja.” The Deity of Lord Govindaji, along with the Deities of Madana-Mohana and Gopinathaji, originally established by Vajranabha in Vrindavana, represent the three eternal duties or in other words the constitutional position of all living entities trapped in the material world under the shackles of maya which are: sambandha, abhdeya, and prayojana. The word abhideya means acting according to that constitutional relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Lord Govindaji is the Deity who helps us to establish this relationship (abhideya) and the siksha-guru or instructing spiritual master acts as the representation of Lord Govinda Deva.

## The Tyrant Aurangzeb Attacks the Govindaji Mandira

It is often said that the temple towered seven stories into the sky, but this referred only to the temple turret, not the entire structure. By observing the architecture of the temple, and other temples of the same design, there would not have been any more than the three floors that are seen today, otherwise the entire architectural beauty of the building would have been lost. In temple architecture, the ratio between the height of the main structure, and the height of the temple turret, must be in conformity with standard temple design mentioned in the Vedas. To calculate the height of the temple turret, which is called the shikara, one must calculate the size of its foundations, therefore, from this measurement one can understand that the height of the temple turret would have been about seven stories, and from this one can also calculate the exact height of the main structure, called the kirtana mandapa, which according to the standard ratio between shikara and mandap, could not have be more than three floors.

More importantly, from the engineering stand-point, there is no superstructure to support any further floors above the three floors that exist today. Another fact is that because the Govindaji Mandira was built during the Mughal era, it combines Hindu, Christian and Islamic architectural traditions. Therefore in Christian traditions a dome is always placed on top of a building to signify its highest point or pinnacle. The kirtana mandapa of the temple is finished with a dome which rises above the height of the third floor, creating in a sense, a forth level, which is surrounded by decorative arches. Similar decorative arches and chattris would also have also run around the roof-top of the third floor, but merely as a decorative embellishment. The large dome above the kirtana mandapa also signifies the sacredness of the Hare-nama kirtana being performed below. It would have been totally against 'Hindu' tradition to build any further floors above the kirtana mandapa, as no one was allowed to place their feet or walk above the kirtana mandapa, where the kirtana was being performed below.

The Govindaji Mandira was built with three turrets; one was the central turret (shikara), which is said to have been seven stories high, with the two smaller turrets on either side. The ground floor contains a number of large and small halls where discourses could be held, or where pilgrims could sit and relax as they do today. The second and third floors were meant as viewing galleries and a place where ladies could have darshana of the Deity and enjoy the kirtanas, without having to mingle with the public on the ground floor where large crowds of men would have normally congregated; where the kirtana exclusively performed by men, would be taking place. Situated on top of the seven story central shikara was a very large oil lamp, which was lit in the evening and fueled with either ghee or oil.

This large oil lamp ultimately led to the destruction of the central shikara when it was spotted by Aurangzeb in far-away Agra, a distance of sixty kilometers south of Vrindavana. Late one evening in the year 1670, the Mughal Emperor, while standing on the ramparts of his fort at Agra, suddenly noticed a bright light in the far distance. After being told it was the light from a Hindu temple in Vrindavana, he became infuriated that the shikara of a temple belonging to Hindu idolaters was far higher than the minaret of a Muslim mosque. In anger Aurangzeb ordered its immediate destruction. Hearing the rumors of an impending attack on Vrindavana by the soldiers of Aurangzeb, the Hindu princes, who had their spies at the Mughal court, sent word to the temple priests in Vrindavana about an imminent attack. Therefore, the priests were able to secretly smuggle the temple Deities out of Vrindavana and take Them to the safety of Rajasthana, which was still ruled by Hindu kings. It was decided to move all the Deities because as soon as Aurangzeb's soldiers would have arrived in Vrindavana, their first target would have been the destruction of these Deities. Thus when the soldiers eventually arrived in Vrindavana they found no Deities.

Aurangzeb's actual order to his soldiers was to dismantle the shikara of the Govindaji Mandira. His soldiers did not actually dismantle any floors of the temple itself accept the easily removable decorative chattris and arches running around the roof-top of the mandap.

Soldiers merely desecrated the temple interior by smashing all the intricate frescos and sculptures they could find, and also defiled the garbha-griha or Deity room, which was sufficient under ancient temple laws for the temple to be abandoned. Aurangzeb's soldiers only dismantled the top four floors of the shikara and then stopped, as Aurangzeb's order had been fulfilled. After dismantling the turrets of the four main temples in Vrindavana the soldiers returned to Agra. This dismantling of the temple turrets has also been confirmed by historical records of the actual episode. The other temples that were desecrated by Aurangzeb's soldiers besides Govindaji were: Madana-Mohana, Radha Gopinath, Jugala Kishore and Radha Vallabha. Since the time of the desecration of Vrindavana's temples, the Deities of the Goswamis have continued to be worshiped in Jaipur. The Deity of Lord Govindaji is presently being worshiped in the grounds of the Jaipura royal palace.

## 40 Venu Kupa / Sixty-four Samadhi Pitha

In the Vraja-riti-cintamani it says, “In the midst of the rasa-dance Radha and Krishna left the gopis company and enjoyed pastimes in a solitary place. When Radha became thirsty, Krishna created this well by playing on His flute.” There were many pastimes where Krishna would suddenly disappear from the gopis taking only Radharani with Him. On some occasions Krishna would also disappear leaving Radharani all alone, but due to the influence of yogamaya, neither Radharani nor the gopis would remember the previous events. The Bhakti-ratnakara says that Krishna created this well to quench the thirst of the cowherd boys. The word 'venu' means 'flute' and 'kupa' means a 'well'. “O Shrinivasa, this is Venu-kupa. Lord Krishnacandra had so much fun at this place. Knowing that His friends were thirsty, Krishna looked at the ground and took His flute in hand. Upon playing on His flute, the sound entered Patalaloka and suddenly there manifested a well filled with water. Krishna's friends all drank that water and then praised Him. Therefore this place is famous in the world as Venu-kupa.” This well which was formerly located on the north-eastern side of the garden containing the Sixty-four Samadhis, has now completely disappeared.

The Sixty-four Samadhi Pitha, which was established at the same time the Govindaji Mandira was built, is primarily a 'smrti-sthala' or 'garden of remembrance' and contains two baithakas (sitting places) belonging to Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda, which are smriti-sthalas and Their Lordships did not actually sit here. These two baithakas are surrounded by the smrti-samadhis of Lord Chaitanya's sixty-four principle followers, who are referred to as the 'Sixty-four Mahantas, the primary leaders of Lord Chaitanya's sankirtana movement and also includes all the Gaudiya Goswamis of Vrindavana. The word 'mahant' generally refers to a temple founder or hereditary administrator. The majority of samadhis are pushpa-samadhis, smriti-samadhis, or nama-samadhis, and in some cases sacred articles like clothing, beads, or garlands belonging to those who are buried here. Amongst the sixty-four samadhis are three full samadhis including the vibhuti-samadhi of Shrila Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami and the full samadhis of Kasishwara Pandita and Subuddhi Raya.

## 40a Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami Samadhi

It is said that Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami would sometimes perform bhajana in this garden near to Venu Kupa whenever he was staying in Vrindavana. This samadhi contains the ashes (vibhuti) of Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami, who disappeared in the year 1579, while performing bhajana on the banks of Radha-kunda where his sacred body was cremated. It was decided to cremate his mortal remains to avoid any chance of desecration in the future by Muslim fanatics. This was also done in the case of both Raghunatha Dasa Goswami and Krishnadasa Kaviraja Goswami, who were also cremated at Radha-kunda. A portion of Radhunatha Bhatta Goswami's ashes were entombed at the Teen Goswami Samadhi Pitha at Radha-kunda.

Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami was born in the year 1505, as the son of Tapan Mishra, a close associate of Lord Chaitanya. When Lord Chaitanya went in His youth to East Bengal to teach Sanskrit grammar, he met Tapan Mishra and advised him to live in Benares (Varanasi). Later when Lord Chaitanya was on His journey from Puri to Vrindavana, he stayed in Benares for a few days at the house of Tapan Mishra and also while in Benares He met another of His associates named Chandrasekhara. While on His return journey, He stayed in the house of Chandrasekhara and took prashadam at Tapan Misra's house. During these visits to Benares, whenever Lord Chaitanya took his meals at the house of Tapan Misra, his young son Raghunatha, who was at that time around ten years old, obtained the Lord's association and had the opportunity to massage the Lord's lotus feet while He rested after His meal. When Lord Chaitanya left for Puri, Raghunatha was so attached to the service of Lord Chaitanya that he wanted to go with the Lord to Puri, but the Lord forbade him to do so as he was still very young.

After completing his studies, Raghunatha finally left for Puri to meet Lord Chaitanya, who was extremely happy to see him and kept him at Puri for about eight months. Raghunatha was a very expert cook and would sometimes prepare meals for Lord Chaitanya. As Tapan Mishra was very old at that time, Lord Chaitanya sent Raghunatha back to Benares to care for his aged parents who were pure Vaishnavas. Lord Chaitanya also advised Raghunatha that he should remain as a life-long brahmachari. After the demise of his parents, Raghunatha returned to Puri staying there in the association of Lord Chaitanya for another eight months. Lord Chaitanya then told him to join Rupa and Sanatana Goswamis in Vrindavana, to assist them in excavating the lost holy places of Krishna's Vrindavana pastimes and propagating the sankirtana movement.

On arrival in Vrindavana, Rupa and Sanatana were very happy to see Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami, and immediately accepted him as their younger god-brother. Raghunatha Bhatta exhibited all the good qualities of a pure Vaishnava and was of very humble demeanor. During the course of his life, he would never hear criticism of others, saying that as they are engaged in Krishna's service, he did not mind their faults. He gained great notoriety for his recitation of the Shrimad-Bhagavatam; his chanting of the Bhagavatam slokas was especially wonderful to hear. His voice was as sweet and melodious as a cuckoo and all those who heard him chanting the sacred slokas became enraptured. He would always recite the Bhagavatam before Rupa and Sanatana and the assembled Goswamis, singing each sloka three or four times over, each time in different meter and raga (tune). During such recitations he would often manifest ecstatic symptoms and his body would shake and his eyes would fill with tears. His hair would also stand on end and his voice would begin to falter, on some occasions he would also swoon. The original Bhagavatam used by Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami has been preserved and can be seen at the Bhattaji Mandira in Vrindavana. He was the spiritual master of Raja Man Singh, the king of Jaipura, and after Emperor Akbar granted permission for the construction of the Goswami temples in Vrindavana, Raghunatha Bhatta asked Raja Man Singh to take charge and supervise all the construction work. According to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, Raghunatha Bhatta Goswami was Raga-manjari in Krishna's Vrindavana pastimes.

## 207 Katyayani Mandira

This temple of Katyayani is one of the famous shakti-pithas of the Shakta sampradaya that primarily worships goddess Duga in her various manifestations. There are as many as fifty-two pithas scattered around India where the various body parts or ornaments of the goddess Sati fell to earth after she was dismembered by the chakra of Lord Vishnu. This is said to be the spot in Vrindavana where ringlets of her hair (katya) fell upon the earth.

There are various legends found in the Puranas that reveal how the Shakti-pithas came into existence. The most popular is based on the story regarding the tragic death of goddess Sati. Out of grief and lamentation, Sati's husband Lord Shiva, while remembering their moments of nuptial bliss together; roamed around the universe carrying Satis dead body in his arms. As Lord Vishnu had cut Satis dead body into fifty-two parts using his sudarshana-chakra, the various parts of Satis body ultimately fell upon the earth at numerous places to become pithams or holy places where the goddess could be worshiped. In another legend it recounts the time when all the demigods gave their celestial weapons (astras) to the goddess in her form as Maha-Kali, in order that she could kill the powerful demon Raktabija and his vast army. Some versions say that the demon was Daruka.. After destroying the demon she could not be stopped in her blood-lust and her furious uncontrollable rampage posed a threat to all life in the universe, including the demigods themselves; it was left to Lord Vishnu to finally cut her to pieces using His weapon known as the sudarshana-chakra, after which Kali's various body parts and ornaments fell to earth.

The worship of the goddess in Hinduism is generally associated with the Tantric tradition of the Matrikas as well as the tradition of the ten Mahavidyas and falls under the broader umbrella of Shaktism. Other famous pithams of the Shakta sampradaya include: Jagannath Temple, Puri, Odisha (Feet). Berhampur, Odisha (Breast) Guwahati, Assam (Yoni) Kalighata, Kolkata, West Bengal (Mouth). Manikarnika Ghata, Varanasi (Earring). Baidyanath, Jharkhand (Heart). Dantewada, Chhattisgarh (Tooth). Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh (Right eye). Kanchi, Tamil Nadu (Naval). It should be noted that this particular temple is not the place where the gopis worshiped goddess Katyayani which was at Chira Ghata near Nanda Ghata some thirty kilometers north of Vrindavana.

## 41 Pani Ghata

This is the famous ghata on the old bank of the Yamuna where the gopis crossed the river without using a boat. According to the Geological Survey of India map, Pani Ghata is located next to Tattiya-sthana, although others have placed it further south near the newly developed Pani Ghata village. However it is said that the entire stretch from Tattiya-sthana southwards is considered to be part of Pani Ghata.

The story of how Radharani and the gopis crossed the Yamuna at Pani Ghata without a boat is related in the Gopala-tapani Upanishad (2.6). Once, Durvasa Muni was observing ekadashi-vrata and was thinking that it would be nice to break his fast on dwadashi with Bhagavata-prashadama. Being the supersoul of all living entities, Krishna understood the mind of the great sage. Therefore, knowing that Durvasa would certainly shower his blessings on anyone who pleased him, Krishna advised Radharani and Her friends to cook a wonderful feast for Durvasa Muni so that he could break his ekadashi fast and suggested that they travel to Panigaon village in order to personally serve the feast to Durvasa Muni who was observing ekadashi-vrata in the vicinity of village. As there were no boats available for crossing the Yamuna to reach Panigaon village, as it sometimes happens in the monsoon season, Radharani asked Krishna how they would be able to cross the Yamuna River to reach the village on the other side. Krishna then told them the secret of how they would be able to cross the river. Therefore, when the gopis reached the Yamuna riverbank, remembering Krishna's words, the gopis prayed to Yamunaji and repeated Krishna's words saying, 'Krishna, the brahmachari'. As soon as the gopis had spoken these words, Yamunaji created a passage for the gopis to cross the river. It would appear that the strong flowing current of the Yamuna subsided revealing a shallow path created by a shifting sand-bar leading through the water to the other side. The gopis then crossed the Yamuna and were able to serve Durvasa Muni with the wonderful feast they had cooked for him. Being extremely pleased with the gopis, Durvasa gave his heartfelt blessings to all of them. Radharani received a special blessing from the sage, that whatever She cooked would always taste like nectar, and whoever ate Her cooking would never become sick and would also live a long life.

The meaning of gopi's statement that 'Krishna is a pure brahmachari' is that Krishna has a spiritual body and is transcendental to all material conditioning like mundane lust; therefore His loving relationship with Radharani and the gopis is based upon pure spiritual emotion or prema-rasa and not connected in any way to mundane sensual activities based on kama or lust, which is in the mode of ignorance. Radharani asked Durvasa Muni how could they again cross the Yamuna, he replied by saying. “Meditate on me as a sage that eats only durva grass and the Yamuna will give you a path.” Reflecting on this advice for a moment, Radharani then asked Durvasa Muni. “How is Krishna sa brahmachari.” Durvasa replied by saying. “In Him we do not find material so-called knowledge and ignorance. Thus ignorance and real knowledge are different. How can Krishna, who is full of real knowledge, become a materialistic enjoyer?”

## 208 Govinda-kunda

Krishna and Balarama used to bring their cows to this kunda to obtain drinking water. As the cows drank the cool waters of the kunda Krishna and Balarama would rest under the shade of the trees while their cowherd boyfriends would massage their legs. It is said that both Rupa and Sanatana Goswamis had at sometime performed their bhajana on the banks of this kunda. Govinda-kunda is the largest of all the kundas found in Vrindavana. The extensive sandstone ghatas surrounding the kunda were built by Princess Chandharani Kali Sundari of Rajshahi (Now in Bangladesh). Unfortunately the kunda is mostly dry throughout the year accept during the monsoon when it fills with rainwater.

Some have said that Shrila Vyasadeva, who took birth near Mathura as the son of Parashara Muni and Satyavati, wrote the tenth-canto of the Shrimad-Bhagavatam here.

## 43 Raja Ghata

This is where Krishna disguised Himself as a boatman to take the gopis across the Yamuna River in His boat. In order to disguise Himself from the gopis, Krishna covered Himself with a large cloak and gopis could not recognize Him. Radharani and the gopis were on their way to sell milk products in a market on the other side of the Yamuna River, but when the gopis arrived at the river-bank, they found there was only one boat owned by a very strange looking boatman dressed in a large cloak. This boatman agreed to take the gopis in his boat, but insisted that before they could ride in His boat, He would first have to bathe the feet of at least one gopi. At first the gopis objected to this proposal, but seeing no other boat in sight, they agreed to the boatman's unusual request, asking which particular gopi's feet the boatman wanted to bathe. The boatman, after some discussion with his boat, chose Radharani, and then very elaborately bathed Radharani's feet with great pomp and ceremony. The boatman then sprinkled the bathing water over his head, and then over his boat, and then over the Yamuna. The gopis were then able to board the boat and the boatman started rowing towards the other shore.

In the middle of the river the boatman suddenly stopped rowing, and complained of weakness due to lack of food. The boatman suggested that the gopis feed him with some of their milk products in order for him to regain his strength so he could continue rowing. At first the gopis refused and threatened to report his behavior to King Kamsa, the powerful ruler of Mathura, but seeing no other alternative, they agreed and fed the boatman with some of their milk sweets, along with some butter and yogurt. After enjoying the milk products, the boatman once again began rowing, but due to being completely bloated by eating so many milk products, the boatman very soon slumped over and lay motionless on the floor of the boat. Radharani asked one of the gopis to see what was wrong with the boatman. Lifting the boatman's cloak to see what the problem was, she suddenly burst out laughing while pulling Krishna's flute from under His waistband. Having discovered the boatman's true identity, all the gopis began laughing and clapping their hands. The gopis then rowed the boat themselves to the other shore.

How To Get There: (See map no.55).

## 44 Mahaprabhu Baithaka / Vishrama Sthali

This is the place where Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu would sit and rest while walking at noon-time from Imli-tala to His camp at Akrura Ghata, as it is the half-way point between the two places. Many years ago there was a roadside shrine located here beneath a large banyana tree, where the Deity of Lord Chaitanys could be seen as pilgrims passed by on the parikrama path. The word 'baithaka' means 'sitting place'. Some refer to this place as Vishrama-sthala, or the resting place of Mahaprabhu, which is also applicable. However, Akrura Ghata is the actual Vishrama-sthala where Mahaprabhu rested at night. There used to be a temple located next to the baithaka containing the Deities of Lord Jagannatha that were once worshiped by Murari Gupta, who was a close associate of Lord Chaitanya. It is said that many years ago, the old and dilapidated former residence of Murari Gupta in Bengal was being renovated, when two sets of Deities were discovered buried in the ground. According to an inscription found at the site, the Deities of Lord Jagannatha and Gaura-Nitai had previously been worshiped by Murari Gupta and both sets of Deities were then sent to Vrindavana to be worshiped in the holy Dhama. The Deity of Lord Jagannatha was installed here at the Chaitanya Baithaka and the Deity of Gaura-Nitai can be seen at the Pishima Gaura-Natai Mandira near Loi Bazar.

How To Get There: (See map no.55).

## Excursion to Other Holy Places 48

Including:\*Jaipur Mandira

## 209 Jaipur Mandira

This is the most grandiose and most architecturally beautiful of all Vrindavana's temples and was built by Raja Sawai Madhav of Jaipur in 1917. The fine hand-carved sandstone is of unparalleled workmanship and it took thirty years to complete the construction. The huge sandstone pillars that support the roof are each carved from one solid rock and in order to haul the large sandstone rocks for the construction of the temple, Raja Sawai Madhava financed the railway line from Mathura to Vrindavana that is still in use even today. The temple has three altars and the Deities being worshiped here are; Shri Shri Radha Madhava, Ananda-bihari and Hamsa-gopala.

How To Get There: (See map no.55).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 45 Davanala-kunda

This was the last place visited by Raghava Pandita, Shrinivasa Acharya, and Narottama Dasa during their parikrama of Vrindavana, which also brought to an end their Vraja Mandala Parikrama. From this place they went to Radha Damodara to meet Jiva Goswami and tell him about all the wonderful places they had visited during the course of their parikrama. The Bhakti-ratnakara says “O Shrinivasa, the same day after chastising Kaliya, Krishna swallowed the forest fire here. Whoever sees this place, known as Davanala-kunda, is relieved from the fire of material life.” This is the celebrated kunda where Krishna extinguished a blazing forest fire. The word 'davanala' means a 'devastating forest fire'. After Krishna had subdued the poisonous Kaliya serpent, because it was already late in the day and darkness was slowly descending, the Vrajavasis decided to spend the night camped out at this place some distance from the Yamuna. During the night, everyone was suddenly awakened by a tumultuous roaring noise that sounded like a large herd of elephants were rampaging through the forest. Suddenly everyone noticed the deadly flames of an enormous forest fire that was rapidly moving towards them. The Vrajavasis thought that their lives were now coming to an end and they all looked toward their beloved Krishna to save them. Krishna was not happy to see the great distress the forest fire was causing to the Vrajavasis and not wasting another moment, Krishna immediately opened his mouth and while inhaling swallowed-up the forest fire in a moment. The Vrajavasis were feeling great relief that Krishna had saved them. After subguing the forest fire Krishna and the Vrajavasis rested for some time at Vishrama-kunda and when dawn approached, they decided it was a good time to leave and everyone happily made their way back to their homes at Sakatikara (Chhatikara).

How To Get There: (See map no. 55 & 55A).

## 46 Radha Kupa

This ancient well known as Radha Kupa or Radha's well, is situated on the Vrindavana parikrama path as it passes through the sub-forest of Viharavana. The well is believed to have been used by Radharani and the gopis for obtaining drinking water when they came to this small forest of Viharavana to enjoy transcendental pastimes with Krishna. The word 'vihara' means 'ambrosial pastimes' and there are a number of temples in Ramana Reti dedicated to the pastimes enacted in Viharavana, one of the twelve upavanas of Vrindavana, which formerly covered the area around Ramana Reti. Unfortunately, this forest no longer exists. The Krishna Balarama Mandira is more or less located at the center where the Viharavana sub-forest once stood.

How To Get There: (See map no.55A).

## Excursion to other holy places 49

Including:\*Krishna Kupa\*Bhagavata-Nivas\*Vishram-kund\*Bhaktivedanta Swami Gate\*Prema Mandira.

## 210 Krishna Kupa

Located in the Bon Maharaja College grounds facing the main road is this ancient well that can be seen from the road. It is said that Krishna Kupa is the place in the sub-forest of Viharavana where Lord Krishna and the cowherd boys used to get drinking water for themselves and their cows.

How To Get There: (See map no.55A).

## 211 Bhagavata Nivas

In this temple one can have darsana the govardhana-sila and gunja-mala that was presented as a gift to Raghunatha Dasa Goswami by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. A devoted follower of Lord Chaitanya known as Sankarananda Saraswati once visited Govardhana Hill and collected a flat yellow-colored govardhana-sila which he gave as a gift to Lord Chaitanya. This shila was worshiped by Lord Chaitanya for three years before He presented it as a gift to Raghunatha Dasa Goswami and ordered him to worship the shila, saying that by serving the rock of Govardhana he will quickly achieve love of God. After the disappearance of Raghumatha Dasa, this particular sila known as Shri Giridhari was worshiped by the daughter of Shrila Ganga Narayana Chakraborty. Eventually this govardhana-sila and gunja-mala was given to Shrila Vishvanatha Chakravarty Thakura to worship during the time that he was performing bhajana at Radha-kunda. When in old age, Vishvanatha Chakravarty moved to Vrindavana, the govardhana-sila was worshiped on the altar of the Radha Gokulananda Mandira. However, this famous sila was secreted away in 1949 by followers of a sidha-pranali babaji-sampradaya who claimed hereditary proprietorship of the shila and brought it to this temple at Bhagavata Nivas where it is still being worshiped even today.

How To Get There: (See map no.55A).

## 212 Vishram-kund

The word 'vishram' means 'to rest' and this small kunda lies hidden inside the Kaladhari Ashram compound. This is the celebrated kunda where Lord Krishna rested along with all the Vrajavasis after He had extinguished the blazing forest fire that was threatening the burn everyone to ashes. After resting at this place overnight, the next morning Krishna and Balarama returned to Sakatikara (Chhatikara) along with Nanda Maharaja, Mother Yashoda, and all the Vrajavasis.

How To Get There: (See map no.55A).

## 213 Bhaktivedanta Swami Gate

This large gate was erected by the Vrindavana Municipality in 1979 in honor of His Divine Grace A.C.Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, the founder-acharya of ISKCON, in recognition of his contribution in spreading the glories of Vrindavana and the teachings of Lord Krishna all over the world. The Vrindavana Municipality also renamed the road leading to Vrindavana as Bhaktivedanta Swami Marg.

How To Get There: (See map no. 55A).

## 214 Prema Mandira

This impressive looking temple was built out of imported Italian marble at a huge cost. The temple was opened in 2011 and has been attracting large crowds as it is one of the first temples when entering Vrindavana from the Delhi highway. The temple has a number of attractions like the Krishna-lila theme park and a colorful musical fountain.

How To Get There: (See map no. 55A).

End of excursion (Return to Vraja Mandala Parikrama route)

## 47 Krishna Balarama Mandira (Iskcon)

This temple was established in the year 1975, by His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, the illustrious founder-acharya of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON). The temple was meant primarily for the benefit of Shrila Prabhupada's thousands of disciples from around the world, who when visiting Vrindavana on pilgrimage, would have their own temple in the holy Dhama where they could stay and take advantage of the unique spiritual atmosphere of Lord Krishna's sacred abode. The Krishna Balarama Mandira now attracts more visitors than any other temple in Vrindavana and is famous throughout India for the exceedingly high standards of Deity worship practiced here in strict accordance with the pancharatrika Vedic rites. The temple is also well known for its pristine cleanliness and very peaceful atmosphere as well as the kirtans and bhajans performed by the Western devotees, which is much appreciated by all those who visit the temple.

One of the most important acharyas in the history of Indian religion, His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, became the first ever 'world teacher' of India's Vedic religion and he single-handedly spread the message of Lord Chaitanya and the chanting of Krishna's holy names to every town and village on the face of the earth. By his efforts 'Hare Krishna' became a regular household word and he himself became world-famous as the founder of the 'Hare Krishna Movement'. Even though advanced in age, he circled the globe fifteen times on lecture tours and initiated thousands of disciples into Krishna consciousness and the practice of bhakti-yoga. In his own lifetime, he established over one hundred temples of Radha and Krishna in almost every major city of the world. He is credited with having ushered in a spiritual revolution that not only changed the lives of millions around the world, but is still continuing to change the lives of millions more, through his innumerable translations and commentaries on the ancient Vedic scriptures that explain the science of devotional service to Lord Krishna.

His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada was the most recent in an unbroken line of Vaishnava acharyas or empowered spiritual masters, stretching back thousands of years that include such great personalities like the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana, Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Shripada Madhavacharya, Sukadeva Goswami, Veda-Vyasadeva, and Narada Muni. His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada was the foremost disciple of Shrila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami, who, as the previous acharya of the Gaudiya Vaisnava sampradaya, gave Shrila Prabhupada the order to take the message of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu to the Western world, in order to give those living outside India the chance to experience the sublime process of Krishna consciousness. Shrila Prabhupada was a highly renowned Vaishnava scholar and his translations of the Vedic classics earned him praise from scholars, theologians, academicians, and religious leaders the world over. His translations of the Vedas are presently used as standard texts in numerous colleges and universities world-wide. His unique translation of the Bhagavad-gita became the best-selling edition in the world, and his books have been translated into more than seventy of the world's major languages with millions of copies of his books having been printed to date; thus Shrila Prabhupada is now recognized as the most prolific author of Vedic religion, culture, and philosophy that has ever lived. In the holy month of Kartik in the year 1977, His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada entered into maha-samadhi at the Krishna Balarama Mandira in Vrindavana and His sacred body was entombed in a very beautiful white marble Samadhi Mandira built by his disciples in the temple grounds.

How To Get There: (See map no. 55A).

End of Vrindavana parikrama & also the end of Vraja mandala parikrama

End of Chapter Nine

## Appendix

## Part One: The Glories of Lord Nityananda

(Adapted from Bhakti-ratnakara)

The two transcendental brothers who previously appeared in Vrindavana as Krishna and Balarama have now appeared in Nadia as Nityananda Prabhu and Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who are one and the same body. Lord Nityananda was born as a brahmana's son in the village of Ekachakra-grama. His father's name was Hridaya Pandita and His mother was Padmavati. To describe the affection for their son is beyond the power of words. Lord Nityananda remained at home for twelve years, during which everyone's affection for Him increased. According to the Bhakti-ratnakara, one day Nityananda considered in His mind, “It is not proper for Me to go to Navadwipa just now. Lord Chaitanya has appeared there and is presently hiding Himself as a child. When He discloses His identity to His devotees, then I will go to meet Him. At present I will go on pilgrimage.”

At that time a sannyasi came to the house of Hridaya Pandita, who became very happy and immediately brought many fine eatables and offered them to him. The sannyasi however said, "I have one request from you. If you accept my request then only I will eat.” Hridaya Pandita immediately agreed and proceeded to feed him. As the sannyasi was leaving he requested Hridaya Pandita to allow his son Nityananda to accompany him. After Hridaya Pandita agreed to the sannyasi's request, Nityananda solaced His parents and then left with the sannyasi. In this way He was able to leave His home. Who can understand Nitai’s wonderful pastimes?

After some time, Nityananda left the company of the sannyasi and travelled alone. Just as He travelled in Dwapara-yuga in the form of Baladeva, now He travelled in the same way to all the holy tirthas. During his travels, Nityananda visited Pandrapura where He saw the Deity of Vithalanatha. In that village lived a very sober brahmana who was a Godbrother of Madhavendra Puri. He took Lord Nityananda to his house and offered Him fruits and milk. Happily seeing the Deity of Vithalanatha, Nitai remained in seclusion in the brahmana's house for many days.

One day the brahmana's guru named Lakshmipati Tirtha, a prominent acharya in the Madhava sampradaya, arrived from a distant place. Who can describe the glories of Lakshmipati Tirtha, whose disciple was Madhavendra Puri. Madhavendra was well known in the Madhva-sampradaya. He was an ocean of transcendental qualities, being very dear to Lakshmipati. For some days Lakshmipati stayed at the house of his brahmana disciple and accepted his food there while passing his time discussing Krishna-katha. On a number of occasions Lakshmipati told his disciple, “There appears to be great auspiciousness in your home and although I have visited previously, I have never felt such happiness in my mind.” Lakshmipati thought to himself that there may be some great devotee also residing within the brahmana's house.

In the evening, while sitting in a secluded place, Lakshmipati spontaneously began singing the glories of Lord Balarama. With unflinching devotion he prayed to Baladeva with tears in his eyes, “O Lord, I am the lowest, sinful person. Please be merciful to me.” After he offered these prayers, he fell to the ground, tears streaming from his eyes. Lakshmipati was very old, and due to his profound loving ecstasy and intense lamentation he was unable to remain steady and fell unconscious. Lord Nityananda, in the form of Balarama, appeared in a dream before Lakshmipati. Speaking slowly He said, “My dear Lakshmipati, My heart breaks hearing your lamentation. Krishna is the Lord of My life and you are His servant life after life.” In the dream, Lakshmipati, holding the lotus feet of Baladeva replied, “I pray that I will never have any other thoughts other than Your Lordship in my mind.” Hearing these words of Lakshmipati, Lord Balarama smiled and said, “In this village, one brahmana's son has come in the dress of an avadhuta. He will become your disciple. With this mantra you initiate Him as your disciple.” Lord Balarama then uttered the mantra in the ear of Lakshmipati who, on receiving that mantra, became ecstatic. After bestowing His mercy, Lord Balarama disappeared.

When he rose in the morning, Lakshmipati began remembering the wonderful dream. Just then Nityananda came before him. Seeing the amazing luster of Nityananda, Lakshmipati began to consider in his mind, “What wonderful bodily effulgence! Surely he cannot be a human being!” Thinking like this, he looked on Lord Nityananda's beautiful face with unblinking eyes. Falling on the ground, Nityananda offered His obeisances to Lakshmipati, who quickly picked Him up and took Him on his lap. Nityananda requested Lakshmipati again and again, “Please initiate Me and deliver Me!” Hearing Nityananda's sweet words, Lakshmipati became agitated and began to float in his own tears. Unable to disobey the order of Lord Balarama, who had appeared in his dream, on that very day Lakshmipati gave initiation to Nityananda. By becoming his disciple, Lord Nityananda increased the ecstasy of His guru.

Very soon after receiving initiation, Nityananda continued with his pilgrimage to the holy tirthas. Being bereft of Nityananda's association, Lakshmipati became greatly agitated. Without speaking to anyone, he thought deeply to himself. As night was ending Lakshmipati fell asleep. In a dream, Nityananda appeared before him and manifested His form of Lord Balarama. Seeing this, Lakshmipati fell at His feet. Wet with his tears, Lakshmipati said again and again, “You have incarnated just to bewilder me. Lord Brahma does not know You, others cannot know You, only those whom You desire can know You. I am a most insignificant insect, a fool. Please show mercy on me for I am surrendered to You.” Hearing the words of Lakshmipati, Lord Balarama again appeared as Lord Nityananda. The form of the Lord was more enchanting than a flashing bolt of lightning. Seeing such beauty, Lakshmipati became immersed in ecstatic love. Lord Nityananda then bestowed His mercy on Lakshmipati. The Lord forbade Lakshmipati to disclose this incident, and after solacing him, disappeared.

Lakshmipati became greatly distressed upon losing the Lord's darshana. He woke from his sleep and saw that night had passed. He was unable to speak to anyone and could not remain patient. From that day onward, due to feelings of acute separation from the Lord, his condition changed drastically. Seeing him in this mood all his disciples became worried. Then suddenly, without warning, Lakshmipati departed their association and went back to Godhead.

According to His own desires, Lord Nityananda travelled to different holy places in great joy. After some days He met Shrila Madhavendra Puri near Pratichi-tirtha on the Mahanadi River. Who can describe the manifestation of love when they met? Only one who has seen can know. Madhavendra Puri accepted Nityananda as his friend, but Nityananda accepted Madhavendra Puri as His guru. In the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Madhavendra Puri states, “Because Lord Krishna has special love for me, therefore I have obtained a friend such as Nityananda.”

After some time Lord Nityananda took leave of Madhavendra Puri and went to Setubandha near Rameshwaram for darshana. Then travelling northward again Lord Nityananda next visited Mathura where He enjoyed playing with the young boys there in the mood of a young cowherd boy. Whoever saw Lord Nityananda just once could not leave His association for a moment. Lord Nityananda is the supreme personification of sweetness. Innumerable people came to see Him. Lord Nityananda, however, did not remain in one place, but wandered throughout Vraja in great ecstasy. Sometimes He would go to Gokula in Mahavana and have darshana of the famous Deity Madana-Gopala where He stayed for some days. When He saw the house of Nanda Maharaja, He would shed tears as He remembered His previous pastimes. Then one day Lord Nityananda departed for Hastinapura, where the Pandavas once resided. He then returned to the forests of Vraja and performed amazing pastimes on the bank of the Yamuna at Rama Ghata. Sometimes He would sit under the beautiful yava tree at Rama Ghata and sometimes He would roll in the dust. Sometimes He would decorate Himself with various flowers and sometimes He would call out, “Where is Kanai, the Lord of My life?” Filled with ecstatic feelings, the body of Lord Nityananda would tremble and His long lotus eyes would fill with tears. Thus the Lord enjoyed His pastimes in Vrindavana. Who has the power to understand His activities?

For twenty years Lord Nityananda travelled to the holy places. Who can describe all the pastimes He performed during that time? However, while staying at Shringara Vata Lord Nityananda could understand that Lord Chaitanya was now manifesting His pastimes in Navadwipa. Lord Nityananda, the wielder of the plow, smiled and in ecstasy and the hairs of His body stood on end. Lord Nityananda became impatient due to His strong attraction towards Lord Chaitanya and immediately departed for Navadwipa.

## Part Two: The Glories of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu

(Adapted from Bhakti-ratnakara)

Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is the eternal Supreme Personality of Godhead, Parambrahma. He is the Lord of Navadwipa, and He is Vrajendra-nandana, the son of Nanda Maharaja. He appeared in Navadwipa in the house of Mother Sachi and Jagannatha Mishra due to the loud calling of Advaita Acharya. The wonderful pastimes of Lord Gauranga cannot be described even by Ananta-Sesha with His one thousand mouths. Lord Chaitanya appeared in Navadwipa in the year 1486, His family name was Vishvambara Mishra, His mother named Him Nimai. In His youth He became a famous scholar of vyakaran and was thus known as Nimai Pandita. Later when He manifested his ecstatic sankirtana pastime He also became known by the names Gaura, Gauranga, Gaurahari, Gaurachandra and Gaurasundara, due to His beautiful bodily features and golden colored complexion.

When His father died, Lord Chaitanya went to Gaya to perform the shraddha ceremony for departed souls. At that time the most fortunate Ishvara Puri regained his life by seeing Gaurachandra. Ishvara Puri was a disciple of Madhavendra Puri, a prominent acharya in the Madhva sampradaya. Gaurasundara is the life of the devotees, thus He offered the greatest affection to Ishvara Puri. Desiring initiation, Lord Chaitanya first spoke His initiation mantra into Ishvara Puri's ear and then, received the mantra back from Ishvara Puri during the initiation ceremony, after which Lord Chaitanya fell on the ground while offering His obeisances to His guru. Thus after accepting Ishvara Puri as His guru, Lord Chaitanya always floated in His own tears while Ishvara Puri became mad with ecstasy after accepting the deliverer of the universe, Lord Vishvambhara, as his disciple.

One may say that Lord Chaitanya is the guru of the entire universe—yet He accepted a guru Himself. This is certainly puzzling. Therefore in order to instruct the people in general, the Lord established the principles of religion by His own example. Who can understand this transcendental pastime of the Lord? He Himself thus glorified the Madhva sampradaya. By accepting a mantra from a bona fide sampradaya one becomes successful. If one receives a mantra from an unauthorized source it will certainly be fruitless. In Kali-yuga there are four authorized sampradayas mentioned as: Shri sampradaya, Brahma sampradaya, Rudra sampradaya and Sanaka \[Kumara\] sampradaya. These four sampraday's are the authorities on the science of bhakti. Lord Chaitanya made the Madhva sampradaya glorious in this Kali-yuga.

Lord Chaitanya was the inaugurator of the Gaudiya sampradaya. Thus the Gaudiya sampradaya became known as the Nimananda sampradaya because Nimai Pandita was the original birth name of Lord Chaitanya. This name Nimai was also very dear to Lord Nityananda. Seeing the Vaishnava devotees of Lord Chaitanya in Bengal, people used to say they were from the Nimananda sampradaya. Because Nimai distributed ananda throughout the world, His sampradaya was known as Nimananda.

After bestowing His mercy on Ishvara Puri, Lord Chaitanya left Gaya and returned to Navadwipa. Previously the Lord used to hide from the devotees in Navadwipa, however, when He returned from Gaya He was unable to hide from them due to His ecstatic mood, although He wanted to. After a few days, upon returning to Nadiya, Gauracandra manifested Himself by the desire of the devotees. All the devotees, headed by Advaita, felt most happy within. When Nityananda arrived from His pilgrimage, that happiness increased. Who can describe it even with millions of mouths? Lord Chaitanya along with Nityananda and Advaita were always immersed in sankirtana and performing the most wonderful activities day after day. After some period of time Lord Chaitanya decided to leave home. The Lord and enchanter of the universe, Gauranga, took to the renounced order of life in order to bestow mercy upon all living entities. He was just twenty-four years old at this time. After taking sannyasa, the Lord became spiritually overwhelmed and therefore Lord Nityananda took Him to the house of Advaita Acharya.

People came rushing from all directions to see Lord Gauracandra, the jewel amongst sannyasis. Demigods along with human beings, together in their millions, came to see the Lord at Advaita Prabhu's house. The residents of the upper, middle, and lower planets became astonished as everyone chanted, 'Hari, Hari!' The jewel of the renounced order, Shri Krishna Chaitanya, made everyone glorious by giving them His darshana. His limbs decorated with sandalwood, Gaurahari danced in ecstasy. All the devotees performed the most pleasing kirtana as they surrounded the Lord on all sides. Nityananda, Advaita, Shrivasa, and Gadadhara, felt ecstatic and were unable to leave the side of Lord Gauranga. Raising His arms, the Lord chanted loudly, 'Hari, Hari!' as He floated in His tears during the ecstatic kirtanas. The people were overwhelmed and forgot themselves by seeing Lord Gauranga in that ecstatic state. After spending some days at the house of Advaita Acharya, Lord Chaitanya left for Puri where He established His permanent residence in the house of Kashi Mishra, who provided a small room known as the Gambhira where Lord Chaitanya could perform his bhajana. During the next few years Lord Chaitanys travelled on pilgrimage to South India, after which He travelled to Vrindavana and inaugurated the vana-yatra, or circumambulation of the twelve sacred forests of Vrindavana Dhama. Lord Chaitanys then returned to Puri where He remained immersed in the transcendental emotions of Radha-bhava until His disappearance in 1534.

## Part Three: Vedic Evidence Proving Lord Chaitanya Was an Incarnation

The incarnation of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the 'Golden Avatara' has been mentioned innumerable times in the Vedic literatures, which proved beyond doubt that He was a genuine incarnation of Krishna. Unless a person is mentioned in the Vedas to be an incarnation, he should not be accepted as such but is in fact an imposter. It is stated in the Chatanya-charitamrita that Lord Chaitanya was a dual incarnation of both Radha and Krishna, “Shri krishna-chaitanya, radha-krishna nahe anya - Lord Chaitanya was an incarnation of Krishna who appeared on earth with the mood and bodily complexion of Radha.” (Cc. Adi 1.5). The Chaitanya-bhagavata says that Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is non-other than the combined form of Shri Shri Radha and Krishna. The scriptures reveal that Lord Krishna desired to experience Radha's own unique spiritual emotions of ecstatic love known as maha-bhava; therefore He appeared on earth in order to relish the unique emotions of Radharani.

The Chaitanya-charitamrita says, “The loving affairs of Shri Radha and Krishna are transcendental manifestations of the Lord’s internal pleasure-giving potency. Although Radha and Krishna are one in Their identity, They separated Themselves eternally. Now these two transcendental identities have again united, in the form of Shri Krishna Chaitanya. I bow down to Him, who has manifested Himself with the sentiment and complexion of Shrimati Radharani although He is Krishna Himself.” (Cc.Adi. 1.5)

The Vedas also refer to Lord Chaitanya as being a 'channa-avatara', or 'hidden-avatara', because although directly Lord Krishna Himself, He appeared as an ordinary human being, thus concealing His true identity from the envious demons of the Kali-yuga. In the Vishnu-sahasra-nama-stotra, recorded in the Mahabharata (Mhb.127.92.75) it says, “In His early pastimes He appears as a householder with a golden complexion. His limbs are beautiful, and His body, smeared with the pulp of sandalwood, seems like molten gold. In His later pastimes He accepts the sannyasa order, and He is equipoised and peaceful. He is the highest abode of peace and devotion, for He silences the impersonalist nondevotees.”

It is stated in the Mundaka Upanishad of the Atharva Veda, “When the sadhaka sees that the Supreme Controller, the sovereign Lord of all potencies and cause of Brahma, in His golden form as the topmost Supreme Being, as the cause of all good fortune - then the sadhaka becoming fully realized and casts far off the reactions to his past pious and sinful activities. Free from all designations, the sadhaka then attains to the stage of equal vision.”

The Chaitanya Upanishad says. “Lord Gaura, who is the all-pervading Supersoul, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, appears as a great saint and powerful mystic who is above the three modes of nature and is the emblem of transcendental activity. He disseminates the cult of devotion throughout the world.”

The Mundaka Upanishad also says, “I am the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Being summoned by the incarnation of Maha-Vishu, Advaita Acharya, I will descend from Goloka-Dhama and appear on the earth planet during the first sandhya of Kali-yuga—in Navadwipa on the banks of the Ganges. I will appear in the form of a brahmana with a large golden complexioned body measuring four hands, endowed with the thirty-two signs of a maha-purusha, and bearing the title Mishra. Then, decorated with all of the auspicious qualities of a maha-bhagavata, endowed with renunciation, devoid of worldly desires, and learned in the science of pure devotional service, I will accept sannyasa, as a devotee relishing the mellows of ecstatic love for Krishna.”

The Shrimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.13) states, “This boy \[Krishna\] has three other colors—white, red and yellow—as He appears in different ages. Now He has appeared in a transcendental blackish color.”

In the Shrimad-Bhagavatam (11.5.32) it also says, “In the age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly sings the name of Krishna. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Krishna Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons, and confidential companions.”

The Shrimad-Bhagavatan \[SB 11.5.34\] also says, “We offer our respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of the Lord, upon whom one should always meditate. He left His householder life, leaving aside His eternal consort, whom even the denizens of heaven adore. He went into the forest to deliver the fallen souls, who are put into illusion by material energy.”

In the Bhagavad-gita (4.8) Krishna declares, “To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of religion, I Myself appear, millennium after millennium.” Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is the deliverer of all the fallen souls. There will never be one more merciful than Him. The yuga-dharma for this age is the congregational chanting of the holy names. By His incarnation, He has happily established this principle of religion.

The Svetasvatara Upanishad (6.7 and 3.12) says, “O Supreme Lord, You are the Supreme Maheshwara, the worshipable Deity of all the demigods and the Supreme Lord of all lords. You are the controller of all controllers, the Personality of Godhead, the Lord of everything worshipable. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is Mahaprabhu, who disseminates transcendental enlightenment. Just to be in touch with Him is to be in contact with the indestructible brahmajyoti.”

The Mundaka Upanishad (3.1.3) also says, “One who sees that golden-colored Personality of Godhead, the Supreme Lord, the supreme actor, who is the source of the Supreme Brahman, is liberated.”

The famous devotee and great Mahajana, Prahlada Maharaja said, “My Lord, You kill all the enemies of the world in Your multifarious incarnations in the families of men, animals, demigods, aquatics and so on. Thus You illuminate the worlds with transcendental knowledge. In the Age of Kali, O Mahapurusha, You sometimes appear in a covered incarnation. Therefore You are known as Tri-yuga \[one who appears in only three yugas\].”

The Krishna-yamala-tantra says, “I shall appear in the holy land of Navadwipa as the son of Sachi Devi.”

The Vayu Purana says, “In the Age of Kali when the sankirtana movement is inaugurated, I shall descend as the son of Sachi Devi.”

The Brahma-yamala-tantra says, “Sometimes I personally appear on the surface of the world in the garb of a devotee. Specifically, I appear as the son of Sachi in Kali Yuga to start the sankirtana movement.”

The Ananta-samhita says, “The Supreme Person, Shri Krishna Himself, who is the life of Shrimati Radharani; He who is the Lord of the universe in creation, maintenance and annihilation, appears as Gaura, O Maheshvara.”

In the Upa-Puranas it is stated, “O learned brahmana, sometimes I accept the renounced order of life to induce the fallen people of the age of Kali to accept devotional service to the Lord.” Because Lord Chaitanya freely distributed the maha-mantra, Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare - all the terrible miseries of the conditioned souls are automatically vanquished. The names: Hari, Krishna, and Rama have wonderful meanings which are relished by the learned devotees. The holy name of the Lord, composed of the thirty-two syllable maha-mantra, is an aspect of transcendental samadhi, as one meditates on the name, form, and pastimes of the Supreme Lord; one develops a deeper understanding of the maha-mantra. The name 'Hare' means the 'internal potency' of Lord Krishna, also referred to as 'hladini-shakti', which is externally manifest in the form of Shrimati Radharani, the eternal consort of Lord Krishna. The name 'Krishna' means 'the reservoir of all pleasure', or in other words the 'Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Shri Krishna'. The name 'Rama' means Lord Krishna, the 'one who gives pleasure to Radha', or in other words Radha-ramana. The Sanskrit word 'rama' means 'pleasure'. Therefore, in the advanced stages of chanting the holy name, one will automatically think of the divine lovers Radha and Krishna as soon as one begins to chant. Thus the maha-mantra is also referred to as being the yugala-mantra as it contains the combined names of both Radha and Krishna.

## Part Four: The Glories of the Holy Name

In the Shrimad-Bhagavatam it says, “In the Age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly sings the name of Krishna. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Krishna Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons and confidential companions.” (SB.11.5.32)

In the Chaitanya-charitamrita it says, “In this Age of Kali, the holy name of the Lord, the Hare Krishna maha-mantra, is the incarnation of Lord Krishna. Simply by chanting the holy name, one associates with the Lord directly. Anyone who does this is certainly delivered.” (Cc.Adi.17.22)

Also in the Chaitanya-charitamrita it says, "The holy name of Lord Rama certainly gives liberation, but the holy name of Krishna transports one to the other side of the ocean of nescience and at last gives one ecstatic love of Krishna." (Anyta.3.257)

The Chaitanya-charitamrita also says, “The word “krish” is the attractive feature of the Lord's existence, and “na” means spiritual pleasure. When the verb “krish” is added to the affix “na”, it becomes “Krishna,” which indicates the Absolute Truth.” (Cc.Madhya.9.30)

The Kali-santarana Upanishad of the Krishna Yajur-veda states: “The sixteen names of the Hare Krsna maha-mantra - 'Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare, Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare' - destroy all the inauspiciousness of the age of Kali. This is the conclusion of all the Vedas.”

In the Brihan-naradiya Purana it says, “For spiritual progress in this Age of Kali, there is no alternative, there is no alternative, there is no alternative to the holy name, the holy name, the holy name of the Lord.” (Cc.Adi.17.21)

In the Ramarcana-candrika it says, “O best of the brahmanas, even without diksha, purascarya, and nyasa-vidhi, simply by chanting the mantras of the Supreme Lord one achieves all perfection.”

The Rama-tapaniya Upanishad (1.6) explains the meaning of the maha-mantra as follows, “The Lord is known as Hari because He takes away the sins and three types of suffering accumulated over millions of births, of those who remember him. The root ‘krish’ indicates the supreme attractiveness of the Lord, the suffix ‘na’ indicates the supreme joy. Thus, the name Krishna indicates the Supreme Brahman who is the acme of these characteristics. The yogis take pleasure in the Supreme Self which is existence, knowledge and bliss absolute. Therefore that truth, known as the Param Brahman is also called Rama.”

In the Brahmanda Purana, Romaharsana Suta offers the following prayer to Shrila Vyasadeva, “O master, O mighty one! Please glorify the Hari-nama mantra situated in transcendence, the cause of all perfection! The embodied soul who accepts this mantra will become filled with transcendence and by accepting it, even a drunkard will attain all perfections. I will recite this mantra to you, for you are a swan-like maha-bhagavata. ‘Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare, Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare.’ These sixteen names can destroy the sins of the three worlds, and nothing higher than them is to be found in all the Vedas.”
