The Agni Purana states, “Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare: Whoever chants this mantra, even neglectfully, will attain the supreme goal of life. Of this there is no doubt.”

The Padma Purana says, “Any Vaishnava who chants the mantra consisting of thirty-two syllables and sixteen names will attain the abode of Radha and Krishna.”

Also in the same Padma Purana there is the following statement on the congregational chanting of the maha-mantra, “Anyone who dances in front of Shri Hari and loudly chants the Hari-nama maha-mantra will destroy all witches of sin. Just as the water of sacred rivers like the Ganga purifies the universe, similarly those who circumambulate Shri Hari and loudly perform nama sankirtana of the 16-word maha-mantra with sweet voices and while clapping the hands, purify the entire universe.”

The Atharva-veda states, “The name is the root of all mantras, the splendid one bringing joy to everyone. This root-mantra is chanted as Hari, Krishna and Rama.”

The Ananta-samhita of the Pancaratra-agamas states, “Hare Krishna Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna Hare Hare, Hare Rama Hare Rama, Rama Rama Hare Hare’ -- This sixteen-name, thirty-two syllable mantra is the maha-mantra in the age of Kali by which all living beings can be delivered. One should never abandon chanting this maha-mantra and take to other so-called purificatory processes which are practiced by rascals, or engage in chanting other metrical compositions of the name of Krishna that are against the pure conclusions of the scriptures, or are filled with rasabhasa. About this divinely spiritual maha-mantra, which delivers one from material existence, the original guru, Lord Brahma, has said, kali-santararadi srutite. ‘The srutis have declared this mantra to be the best means of deliverance in the age of Kali'. Having all heard this from Brahma, the sons and disciples of Brahma, beginning with Narada, all accepted the Hare Krishna maha-mantra, and having meditated on it, attained perfection.”

In the Jnanamrita Sara, of the Pancaratrika it says, “Located next to him (the guru), the disciple should hear the sixteen names of Hari from his mouth, thus taking shelter of the mantra which protects from inauspiciousness and causes auspiciousness for the three worlds.”

In the Brahma Yamala, the following statement is found, “Without Hari, there is no way to eradicate the sins of the age of Kali, and therefore it is essential that Hari-nama should be manifest in all the worlds. In this way the entire world can be delivered from the great sins of the age of Kali. First one should twice chant ‘Hare Krishna’, then twice ‘Krishna, then twice 'Hare', then twice 'Hare Rama’, and in the end, O Maha-Devi, one should chant 'Rama' twice, and then 'Hare Hare'. In this way one should pronounce Krishna's Hari-nama maha-mantra, which destroys all sins.”

In the Chaitanya-charitamrta (Adi. 17.22) it says, “kali-kale nama-rupe krishna-avatara, nama haite haya sarva-jagat-nistara - In this Age of Kali, the holy name of the Lord, the Hare Krishna maha-mantra, is the incarnation of Lord Krishna. Simply by chanting the holy name, one associates with the Lord directly. Anyone who does this is certainly delivered.”

## Part Five: The Glories of Shrimati Radharani

"The beauty of Shrimati Radharani's eyes forcible devours the beauty of the newly grown blue lotus flower, and the beauty of Radha's face surpasses that of an entire forest of fully blossomed lotuses. Radha's bodily luster seems to place even gold in a painful situation. Thus the wonderful unprecedented beauty of Shrimati Radharani is awakening in Vrindavana." (Vidagdha-madhava)

"O Radharani, O Queen of Vrindavana, Your complexion is like molten gold, Your doe-like eyes are captivatingly restless, a million full and brilliant moons wane before Your lustrous countenance, and a blue sari, having stolen the hue of a fresh rain-laden cloud, has enwrapped Your exquisite form. O Radha, You are the crest-jewel of all the dallying damsels of Vrindavana, fragrant and pristine like a budding jasmine flower. Your sublime form is adorned with priceless jewelry, and you are the best of all the charming and intelligent gopis. You are decorated with all wonderful excellences and surrounded by eight dedicated and beloved cowherd girls known as the ashta-sakhis. The ambrosia of Your beautiful lips, red as the bimba fruit, is life-giving syrup to Krishna. O Radha, I am rolling on the banks of the Yamuna, my poor heart filled with anticipation, praying to You with all humility. I am guilty of being an offender, a rascal, a useless wretch -- yet I beg You to kindly engage me in even the smallest service to Your lotus feet. O most merciful Lady, it will not become You to ignore this most distressed soul, for Your heart is always overflowing with compassion and love." (Stavamala - Shri Prarthana-paddhati)

"The transcendental goddess Shrimati Radharani is the direct counterpart of Lord Shri Krishna. She is the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune. She possesses all the attractiveness to attract the all-attractive Personality of Godhead. She is the primeval internal potency of the Lord." (Brihad-Gautamiya Tantra)

“Unadulterated acts of the hladini-shakti are displayed in the dealings of the damsels of Vraja. Shrimati Radharani is the topmost participant in that transcendental group. The essence of hladini-shakti is love of Godhead. The essence of love of Godhead is called bhava, transcendental sentiment, and the highest pitch of that bhava is called maha-bhava.” (From an essay on Chaitanya-charitamrita by Shrila Prabhupada)

"Amongst the damsels of Vraja, Shrimati Radharani and Chandravali are the principal factors. Out of these, Shrimati Radharani is better in all respects. She is the embodiment of maha-bhava and no other gopi possesses such transcendental qualities." (Ujjvala-nilamani)

“Shrimati Radharani always keeps Her hand on the shoulders of Her friends and Radha always talks and thinks of the pastimes of Krishna. Radharani forever offers Krishna a kind of intoxication by Her sweet talks. Shri Radha supplies all the demands of Shri Krishna, and Radharani possesses unique and uncommon qualities meant for Krishna’s satisfaction. Shrimati Radhika is able to fulfill all the desires of Krishna. No one else can do so. Radha is so expert in all affairs that the damsels of Vraja come to learn the arts from Her.” (The Teachings of Lord Chaitanya. Ch.31)

"The plenary expansions of Krishna’s personality are called vaibhava-vilasa and vaibhava-prakasha, and Radha’s expansions are similarly described. The goddesses of fortune are Her vaibhava-vilasa forms, and the queens are Her vaibhava-prakasha forms. The personal associates of Radharani, the damsels of Vraja, are direct expansions of Her body. As expansions of Her personal form and transcendental disposition, they are agents of different reciprocations of love in the pastimes of Lord Krishna, under the supreme direction of Shrimati Radharani. In the transcendental realm, enjoyment is fully relished in variety. The exuberance of transcendental mellows is increased by the association of a large number of personalities similar to Radharani, who are also known as gopis or sakhis. The variety of innumerable mistresses is a source of relish for Shri Krishna, and therefore these expansions from Shrimati Radharani are necessary for enhancing the pleasure potency of Shri Krishna. Their transcendental exchanges of love are the superexcellent affairs of the pastimes in Vrindavana. By these expansions of Shrimati Radharani’s personal body, She helps Lord Krishna taste the rasa dance and other, similar activities." (Chaitanya-charitamrita Adi 4.81, Purport)

Shrimati Radharani Possesses Twenty-five Transcendental Attributes

1\)    Radharani is very sweet and most charming to look at;

2\)    Radha is adolescent and always freshly youthful;

3\)    Radhika’s eyes are doe-like and restless;

4\)    Shri Radha’s face is smiling and every blissful’;

5\)    Auspicious, beautiful lines adorn Shri Radha’s lotus hands and feet;

6\)    Radharani maddens Krishna with Her fragrant bodily aroma;

7\)    Shrimati Radharani is the most exceptional singer and vina player;

8\)    Radha’s words are charming and pleasing;

9\)    Radha is expert at telling jokes that delight Krishna;

10\)   Shrimati Radhika is exceptionally humble;

11\)   Radha is the embodiment of mercy and compassion;

12\)   Shri Radha’s intelligence and wit surpasses all;

13\)   Radharani is expert at performing all activities of love;

14\)   Shyness is the shining gem in Radha’s character;

15\)   Radharani is the beacon light of modesty and never swerves from the path of honesty;

16\)   Radha is never perturbed by worldly sorrow or misery;

17\)   Radharani has unbounded gravity and sublimity;

18\)   Radhika is ever fascinated to unite Herself with Krishna;

19\)   Radha possesses mahabhava, the highest sentiments of love;

20\)   Radharani is the reservoir of loving affairs in Gokula;

21\)   Radha’s transcendental glories are shining in all the worlds;

22\)   Shri Radha is most affectionate to Her superiors;

23\)   Radhika is submissive to the love of Her senior girlfriends;

24\)   Radharani is the chief among Krishna's gopi lovers;

25\)   Radha always keeps Krishna under Her control and He submissively obeys Her command.

## Part Six: The Appearance of the Yamuna River on Earth

The following verses from the Garga Samhita describe the appearance of the river goddess Shrimati Yamuna Devi in the land of Vraja Bhumi. “As the Original Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krishna, who is the king of Goloka and the master of countless universes was about to depart in order to remove the earth's burden, He said to Radha: "O beloved, do not be afraid. You should also go to the earth." Shri Radha said: "My heart cannot be happy in a place where there is no Vrindavana forest, no Yamuna River, and no Govardhana Hill." Sri Sannanda said: "Then Lord Hari sent a 47 krosa portion of His own abode, along with Govardhana and the Yamuna, to the earth." Garga samhita (2.2.5-8)

“Ordered by Lord Krishna in Goloka, Yamuna, the best of rivers, circumambulated the Lord and was about to go to the earth. Then the Viraja river and the spiritual Ganga river both entered the Yamuna. O king Nanda, for this reason the people know that the Yamuna is the greatest of rivers and the first queen of Lord Krishna. Then, with great force breaking through the current of the Viraja, the Yamuna left the gate of the transcendental forest grove. Touching countless universes, she came to the Ganga. With great force the great Yamuna river broke through the Ganga's waters. Then the Yamuna came to an opening Lord Vamana's left toe had made in the top of a universe, an opening through which the Ganga flowed. With Shri Ganga entering that opening, the Yamuna, the best of rivers, then came to the unconquerable Lord's abode of Vaikuntha in the planet of Maharaja Dhruva. Then the Yamuna came to Brahmaloka. Falling from Brahma's planet, she went to the hundreds of planets of the demigods. She went from one planet to another. Then with great force she fell on Mount Sumeru. Flowing from its peaks, she broke the stones on its slope. Then, in order to go south from Mount Sumeru, Shri Yamuna left Shri Ganga's path. Then the Ganga went to Mount Himavat and the great river Yamuna went to Mount Kalinda. Because she is thus Mount Kalinda's daughter, she is named Kalindi. Flowing from Mount Kalinda's peaks, and breaking the hard rocks on his slopes, the sacred Kalindi swiftly flowed on the earth, purifying the countries she passed. Then she entered the Khandava forest.” Sri Garga samhita (2.3.1-13)

NOTE: While loitering in the Kandhava Forest, Kalindi (Yamuna) saw Lord Krishna and desired to become His wife. Kalindi humbly petitioned Arjuna who helped to get Krishna as her husband.

“Wishing to attain Lord Krishna, the Original Supreme Personality of Godhead, as her husband, Kalindi assumed a splendid spiritual form and performed great austerities. Even today she stays in a water-house her father made for her. Then the Kalindi swiftly entered Vraja-mandala. Then she flowed through Vrindavana, beautiful Mathura, and beautiful secluded Mahavana. As the very beautiful leader of many gopis, Sri Yamuna made her home in Vrindavana to eternally perform the rasa-dance with Sri Krishnacandra.”

Garga Samhita (2. 3.14-17)

Shri Yamuna-sahasra-nama-kathana (Adapted from the Garga Samhita)

“Shri Yamuna contains all holy places within her waters (sarva-tirthamayi and tirtha), makes the holy places sacred (tirthanam tirtha-karini), removes all sins (harini sarva-dosanam), gives all good fortune (dayini sarva-sampadam), and is a kala expansion of Lord Krishna (Kala). Shri Yamuna is the daughter of Mount Kalinda (kalindi). She is dark (krishna), has a dark form (krishnarupa), she is eternal (sanatani) and was born from Lord Krishna's left shoulder (krishna-vamamsa-sambhuta) and has a form of transcendental bliss (paramananda-rupini). She resides in Goloka (goloka-vasini), is dark (syama), enjoys pastimes in Vrndavana (vrindavana-vinodini), is Radha's friend (radha-sakhi), dances in the rasa-lila (rasa-lila), and is an ornament in the rasa-dance circle (rasa-mandala-mandani). She stays in the forest groves (nikunja-vasini) and is graceful as a flowering vine (valli and ragga-valli), she is beautiful (manohara) and stays in the rasa-dance circle (sri-rasa-mandali-bhuta), is a gopi (yuthi-bhuta) and is Lord Krishna's beloved (hari-priya). She stays in Goloka (goloka-tatini) and is most glorious (divya), she stays in the forest (nikunja-tala-vasini), is very long (dirgha) and filled with great waves and currents (urmi-vega-gambhira), and decorated with flowers and leaves (puspa-pallava-vahini). She is as dark as a cloud (ghana-cyama), is dark like a garland of clouds (meghamala), she is the home of many cranes (balaka) and is garlanded with many lotus flowers (padma-malini), she is the most perfect (paripurnatama), is perfect (purna) and is the perfect Supreme Personality of Godhead's beloved (purna-brahma-priya), and is completely transcendental (para). She is very powerful (maha-vegavati), she stands at the entrance to Vrndavana forest (saksan-nikunja-dvara-nirgata), she is a great river (maha-nadi) and very gentle (manda-gatir) and she very easily eclipses the celebrated Viraja River (viraja-vega-bhedini).” Sri Garga Samhita (2.19.4-9)

“Yamuna is a moat surrounding the spiritual world (vaikuntha-parikhi-bhuta and parikha), removes sins (papa-harini), she stays in the spiritual world (brahmaloka-gata, brahmi, svarga, and svarga-nivasini), is splendid and playful (ullasanti), is filled with great waves (protpatanti), and is glorious as a garland of Mount Merus (meru-mala), she is very glorious (mahojjvala), is more sacred than the Gagga (shri-gaggambhah-shikharini), flows with such force that she breaks great boulders (ganda-caila-vibhedini), purifies the lands where she flows (decan punanti), flows swiftly (gacchanti and vahanti), flows on the earth (bhumi-madhya-ga), is the sun-god's daughter (martanda-tanuja), is sacred (punya), is Mount Kalinda's daughter (kalinda-giri-nandini), and is Yamaraja's sister (yama-svasa), she smiles gently (manda-hasa), has beautiful teeth (su-dvija), wears beautiful garments (racitambara), wears blue garments (nilambara), has a lotus face (padma-mukhi), walks gracefully (caranti), is beautiful to see (caru-darsana), has thighs graceful as banana trees (rambhoru), has lotus eyes (padma-nayana), is Lord Krishna's beloved (madhavi), is the best of beautiful women (pramadottama), is austere (tapac-caranti), has beautiful hips (su-croni), wears tinkling anklets and belt (kujan-nupura-mekhala), stays in the water (jala-sthita), has dark limbs (syamalaggi), is sweet as khandava-candy (khandavabha), and is playful (viharini), she spoke to Arjuna (gandivi-bhasini), is filled with sacred water (vanya), desires Lord Krishna as her husband (sri-krishnam varam icchati), stays in Dwaraka (dwarakagamana), and is Lord Krishna's queen (rajni, pattarajni, and maha-rajni), she attained the Supreme Personality of Godhead as her husband (paraggata), wears jewel ornaments (ratna-bhusa), is glorious (gomati), is a great river (tira-carini), is Lord Krishna's wife (swakiya), is happy (sukha), has attained her desires (svartha), fulfills the desires of they who worship her (sva-bhakta-karya-sadhini), has a youthful form (navalagga), is a beautiful girl (abala, mugdha, and varagga), has beautiful eyes (vama-locana), and is eternally young (ajata-yauvana), she is humble (dina), is glorious (prabha-kanti, dyuti, cchavi, and su-cobha), is transcendental (parama), is famous (kirti), is beautiful and auspicious (kucala), and is a girl whose eternal youth cannot be understood by conditioned souls (ajnata-yauvana).” Garga Samhita (2.19. 12-20)

**Yamuna Devi and Her Many Manifestations**

Yamuna Devi is directly the daughter of the sun-god Surya-Narayana and the sister of Yamaraja, thus the two siblings are sometimes referred to as Yama and Yami. The scriptures say that Yamuna Devi is eternally in the form of a blossoming youth and has the most beautiful features with a dark complexion (shyama) exactly like that of Lord Krishna. Besides her personal form as a divine goddess, she has manifested herself as the sacred river Yamuna. The Garga Samhita says that both the celestial rivers known as the Viraja and the Ganges, have entered the Yamuna as she descended to earth from the spiritual world. Yamuna is also known as Kalindi because she falls to earth on the mountain top known as Kalinda in the high Himalayas, therefore she is sometimes said to be the daughter of the Kalinda Mountain. She also appears as a gopi and performs transcendental pastimes like rasa-lila with Krishna in the forest of Vrindavana. Yamuna also manifests as Princess Kalindi, one of Krishna's queens in Dwaraka. Besides this, in the Yamuna-sahasra-nama, Yamuna Devi is said to be an expansion of Krishna. “Yamuna is a kala expansion of Lord Krishna” The Yamuna-sahasra-nama also says that Yamuna was born from Lord Krishna's left shoulder. The Padma Purana also says that Yamuna is an expansion of Krishna when it says. “Krishna exists in the form of Yamuna.” According to some authorities the Yamuna River is an expansion of Shrimati Radharani and others say that Yamuna is an expansion of the gopi Chandravali. Some of the acharyas of the Gaudiya sampradaya have said that Yamuna is a manifestation of Vishakha Devi, one of the ashta-sakhis, the most confidential serving maids and close friends of Shrimati Radharani.

In his book Jaiva-dharma Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura describes the Yamuna River as follows: "Yamuna - a sacred river flowing through Vraja-mandala. She is considered the holiest of rivers because Krishna performed many sublime lilas in her waters with the gopis and gopas. In this world she appears at Yamunotri in the Himalayas. Yamuna is described as an expansion of Vishakha Devi: “visakhorasi ya vishnor yasyam vishnur jalatmani nityam nimajjati pritya tam saurim yamunam stumah - Lord Visnu daily immerses Himself and plays with great pleasure and affection in the water of Yamuna, the liquid form of Vishakha Devi. Thus I offer prayers to Yamuna Devi, the daughter of Surya." (Jaiva-dharma, Glossary of Places, the Yamuna River).

Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana says that Yamuna is the embodiment of Vishakha and in one of his verses glorifying Yamuna he says. “vishakha yamuna-vapur iti vicarena yamuna-stutya tat stutir iti vidyabhusana - Sri Vishakha is considered as the vapu (embodiment) of Yamuna. Therefore, by offering prayers to Yamuna one is thus offering prayers to vishakha."

It is not very difficult to comprehend why it might be said that Yamuna is an expansion of Radharani. This is because Vishakha is herself an expansion of Radharani. The truth is that Radharani has expanded Herself to become the various groups of gopis like the ashtha-sakhis as well as Chandravali and her friends, with each gopi possessing their own unique beauty, nature and qualifications, so as to increase the transcendental pleasure experienced by Krishna while performing His madhurya-lila pastimes.

**The Glories of the Yamuna River**

In the Sri Yamunashtakam Shrila Rupa Goswami says, "Sprinkling a single drop of her water upon oneself destroys the reaction of most heinous crimes. She increases the flow of confidential devotional service (raganuga-bhakti) for Nandanandana (Krishna) within one’s heart and blesses everyone who simply desires to reside on her banks. May Yamunadevi, the daughter of Suryadeva, always purify me."

The Bhakti-ratnakara says, “O Srinivasa, who can describe the numerous glories of Shri Yamuna? Bathing in the Yamuna at Mathura gives one a hundred times superior results to those obtained from bathing in the Ganga.”

This is confirmed in the Adi-varaha Purana as follows, “Within My Mathura-mandala the famous Yamuna is one hundred times superior to the Ganga. One should not argue about this. O sinless goddess, I have many confidential sacred places along the Yamuna. Whoever takes bath there becomes worshipable in My abode.”

In the Matsya Purana, in a conversation between Yudhishtira and Narada, it is stated, “O Yudhishtira, a man becomes virtuous if he takes a bath in the Yamuna, drinks the pure water and sings her glories. Even the darshana of Yamuna gives auspicious results. One who takes bath in the Yamuna or drinks her water guarantees auspiciousness for seven generations of his family. Whoever dies on the bank of the Yamuna attains the eternal abode.”

In the Vishnu Dharmottara it is stated, “O King, whoever performs the shraddha ceremony on the bank of the Yamuna attains immortal results and becomes happy in heaven.”

In the Bhakti-ratnakara it says, “According to the Puranas, one achieves superior fruits by taking bath in Yamuna at special times. O Shrinivasa, it is commonly known that by the mercy of Yamuna one can easily fulfill his desires. As iron becomes gold by the touch of the touchstone, so a sinful person becomes virtuous by the touch of the waters of the Yamuna.”

In the Vraja-ritti-cintamani Shrila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura says, “They who offer respectful obeisances to her or bathe in her waters, the Yamuna, which is like a moat of black mascara encircling Vrindavana, transforms them into pure devotees carrying Lord Krishna in their hearts. The Yamuna river is like a blue lotus flower garland, a sapphire necklace, or a blue sash worn by the goddess of Vrindavana.”

In the Padma Purana it says, “A person who takes a holy dip in Yamuna becomes liberated from all his sorrows. The virtue acquired by taking a bath in Yamuna is greater than paying visits to various holy places like Pushkar, Kurukshetra, Brahmavarta and Kashi. Taking a dip in Yamuna also helps in the fulfillment of all the desires of a man. Although, different rituals have been attributed to various yugas like Saytayuga--penance, Treta--Knowledge, Dwapara--yagya and Kali--donation, yet virtue of taking a holy dip in Yamuna transcends even time."

## Part Seven: Philosophical Truths Regarding the Marriage of Radha and Krishna

This incident of the marriage ceremony between Radha and Krishna was enacted specifically for the pleasure of Lord Brahma and the demigods. This pastime fulfilled their desire to see Radha and Krishna married together in a wedding ceremony in accordance with the standard social customs of Vedic culture. This was because Lord Brahma knew in the future that the divine pastimes of parakiya-rasa revealed by Radha and Krishna on the earthly plane, would be severely criticized and misunderstood by mundane moralists and so-called religionists, and therefore to preempt all false criticism, Lord Brahma personally performed Their marriage ceremony while Radha and Krishna were still in Their infancy.

According to Gaudiya Vaishnava philosophy as propounded by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Shri Shri Radha and Krishna, in Their original manifested forms are not married, but remain as eternal lovers in the mood of parakiya-bhava, which means a conjugal relationship as paramours. This is because the super-excellent parakiya-bhava provides the greatest transcendental pleasure for Radha and Krishna and is therefore regarded as the most superior form of bhava, or loving mood within the category of madhurya-rasa, which is itself considered the most superior amongst the five essential rasas. Another point is that at the time of this ceremony at Bhandiravana, both Radha and Krishna were still only about two or three years old and enjoying Their kaumara-lilas, or pastimes as little children at Gokula and Ravala respectively. This manifestation of the wedding ceremony at Bhandiravana was certainly a unique spiritual event similar to the secret manifestation of the Yoga-pitha.

This parakiya-bhava is only experienced by Krishna and the gopis, whereas the queens at Dwaraka headed by Rukmini, although they also enjoy the madhurya-rasa in a conjugal relationship with Krishna as His wives, cannot experience the emotions of parakiya-bhava. This is because when lovers marry and live together at home; the mood of separation and expectation of meeting is lost, being replaced with a feeling of happiness, fulfillment, and complete contentment. But if one's lover, through unforeseen circumstances, marries another, the lovers then experience acute pain in separation and meetings become extremely difficult and can only be undertaken in secret. This greatly heightens the expectation of meeting one's lover, as well as the pleasure derived from it, thus adding further intrigue to the relationship between the lovers, not found in marriage. Therefore, parakiya-bhava is greatly superior, due to the intense emotions that are experienced by the lovers.

This marriage ceremony between Radha and Krishna at Bhandiravana was for the pleasure of the demigods which fulfilled their desire to see Radha and Krishna married. In this regard, in order to give pleasure to the gopis, Krishna was 'married' to all the prominent gopis at one time or another during His various pastimes in the forests of Vrindavana. In the Gopala-champu, it is also said that when Krishna returned from Dwaraka to meet all the Vrajavasis, in order to give pleasure to Yashoda Mayi and Nanda Maharaja, He was married to Radha as well as to all the gopis who took part in the Vraja-lila pastimes.

This so-called marriage between Radha and Krishna also satisfies the needs of the mundane moralists, who find great difficulty in accepting the so-called immoral parakiya relationship between Radha, a married woman, and Krishna, Her secret lover. Even Mahatma Gandhi, who was a staunch believer in the Bhagavad-gita, once admitted that he found it very difficult to reconcile Krishna's so-called immoral behavior with the gopis of Vrindavana. This also proves the point that unless one takes shelter of a bona-fide spiritual master, even if one reads the Gita throughout his entire life, he is unable to comprehend the actual truth about Krishna's transcendental pastimes.

Besides the mundane moralists, a number of so-called sampradayas have sprung up in Vrindavana, propagated by so-called rasikas, who attempt to invent some new philosophy to suit their own misconstrued understanding, and thus try to counteract the supposed contradictions of the parakiya-vada. Prominent amongst them are the followers of Hit Harivamsa of the Radhavallabha sampradaya, Vallabha Bhatta of the Vallabha sampradaya, and Haridasa Swami of the Sakhi sampradaya. None of these so-called rasika-sampradayas follow the traditional science of bhakti-yoga based strictly upon revealed Vedic scripture. They also misconstrue the teaching of the four authorized sampradayas, or schools of Vedic philosophy, and are unable to recognize who are the bona-fide acharyas. Krishna Himself has established the four bona-fide Vedic sampradayas and He has clearly said in the Bhagavata-gita. “Evam parampara praptam.” This means that one should try to learn the truth by approaching an empowered acharya belonging to a bona-fide Vedic sampradaya that has descended directly from Krishna Himself, who is the original acharya, or spiritual master.

These so-called rasika-sampradayas have instead been based solely upon the sentimental poems and songs of their founders, and thus have no genuine shastric or scientific support. Although some of them even claim allegiance to one or more of the bona-fide sampradayas, this is just a ruse to gain acceptance, even though they do not strictly follow those particular sampradaya's precepts or principles. Besides this, they all propagate many false and materialistic concepts including the caste-goswami system also referred to in the shastras as jati-gosai, listed amongst the twelve devious apa-sampradayas that are followed exclusively by the prakrita-sahajiyas. The word ‘sahajiya' means 'one who takes things cheaply' and ‘prakrita' means 'materialistic', or in other words, someone whose mind has not been purified of lust, even after having taken to the path of Krishna-bhakti, and who utilize religion in order to achieve their own gross sensual pleasures in the form of sex, money, false prestige, and followers.

Instead of accepting Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the prakrita-sahajiyas want to compete with Him and claim for themselves grandiose titles like: mahaprabhu, mahaparusa, maha-bhagavata and rasikacarya. It is a proven fact that unless one surrenders and takes shelter of Krishna's direct incarnation who appeared in Kali-yuga in the form of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and accepts the teachings and philosophy of the Gaudiya Vaishnava sampradaya that He founded, no one can become a pure maha-bhagavata devotee, or true rasika, what to speak of understanding rasa-tattva, or the divine emotions of the parakiya-bhava of Radha and Krishna. The Vedic scriptures have revealed that Lord Chaitanya Mahapabhu is the direct incarnation of Krishna, who appeared on earth as the ‘Golden Avatara' and exhibited exactly the same bhava, as well as the golden complexion as Radharani Herself. The scriptures also reveal that Krishna incarnated as Lord Chaitanya in order to understand the unfathomable love that Radharani possesses, as well as to spread the yuga-dharma of nama-sankirtana, or congregational chanting of the holy names of the Lord. It was also Lord Chaitanya who revealed for the first time, the transcendental states of ecstatic love known as gopi-bhava and maha-bhava that had never been scientifically explained before in the history of the Vedic culture. If someone is unable to even recognize the direct incarnation of Krishna when He appears on earth in the divine form of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, how can they possibly proclaim themselves as great devotees of Radha and Krishna, what to speak of falsely claiming to be on the same spiritual level as a Vaishnava rasikacharya, or maha-bhagavata.

## Part Eight: Philosophical Truths Regarding Lakshmi’s Penance

There is a Vrajavasi folklore which says that Lakshmi Devi was not successful because She did not take direct shelter of Radharani, due to being proud of Her own position as the Goddess of Fortune and the untold opulence at Her command, She instead decided to go to Bilvavana thinking that by the strength of Her severe tapasya, She would be able to enter the rasa-lila. But unfortunately, even after performing tapasya for a very long time, she could not become a gopi because She did not take shelter of Radharani.

However, this Vrajavasi folklore is only partly true because one cannot take direct shelter of Radharani, or any of the gopis, without first obtaining the mercy of a bona-fide spiritual master in disciplic succession, only then can one become eligible to take shelter of Radharani or the gopis. Lord Krishna has given His own instructions in the Bhagavad-gita (4.34) regarding advancing in spiritual life as well as achieving the position of a gopi in Vrindavana when He says, “Just try to learn the truth by approaching a spiritual master. Inquire from him submissively and render service unto him. The self-realized souls can impart knowledge unto you because they have seen the truth.” This verse from the Bhagavad-gita means that one should try to learn the truth by taking shelter of Krishna's representative, the bona-fide spiritual master, who already knows the truth because he himself has followed the process and become successful. Without any doubt Shrimati Radharani favors those who follow Krishna's instructions and who take shelter of an authorized spiritual master in disciplic succession from Krishna, not those who neglect Krishna's instructions and try to approach Radharani or the gopis directly. Accepting a bona-fide spiritual master is the first principle if one wants to become a gopi. Unfortunately there is a class of persons called prakrita-sahajiyas who neglect the instructions of Bhagavad-gita and other Vedic literatures and attempt to approach Radharani and the gopis directly. But they also fail in their attempt because of neglecting Krishna's instructions by not first taking shelter of a spiritual master in disciplic succession.

A further consideration is that sometimes these Vrajavasi folklores are accepted as 'Absolute Truth' by the sahajiyas and so-called rasikas, who jump straight to the tenth canto of the Shrimad-Bhagavatam and are completely ignorant of the injunctions of the shastras. They foolishly think that they are qualified to directly approach Radharani, or the gopis such as Lalita. This false conception that one can directly approach Krishna or Radharani, or any of the gopis, is directly opposed to the conclusions of the Vedic shastras and against the mood of pure devotional service to Radha and Krishna.

When Lord Chaitanya visited Shrirangam and stayed at the house of Vyenkatta Bhatta, a worshiper of Lakshmi-Narayana, one day the Lord asked Vyenkata Bhatta as to why Lakshmidevi wanted to be with Krishna?" And also why did She fail in her endeavor even after performing so much penance. Vyenkatta Bhatta was at a loss as to the answer. Lord Chaitanya then explained that Lakshmidevi wanted to remain in Her position as the opulent goddess of fortune in Vaikuntha and at the same time enter into the pastimes of Krishna, where sweetness and beauty are superior to power and opulence. This is not possible. Only those who follow in the footsteps of the gopis and the residents of Vrindavana can attain such a position. Lakshmidevi failed because She did not follow in the footsteps of the gopis.

Just to set the proper example, when Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the direct incarnation of Krishna, appeared on earth along with the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana who were all eternally liberated nitya-siddha devotees, each and every one of them, including Lord Chaitanya Himself, accepted a bona-fide spiritual masters in disciplic succession just to show the bona-fide method of following in the footsteps of the gopis.This is why they and the followers of the Gaudiya sampradaya have been so successful in spreading the glories of Vrindavana and the holy names of Radha and Krishna all over the world. This is the real proof that they have achieved the mercy of Radharani, otherwise how could they have done it. On the other hand, the sahajiyas and so-called rasikas could achieve nothing, even though they certainly tried very hard. The real proof of having achieved the mercy of Radharani can be judged by how successful one has been in spreading the glories of Radharani and how many people one has influenced to surrender their lives to the service of Radha and Krishna and the chanting of the holy name. The conclusion is that because the Six Goswamis and their associates were all eternally liberated nitya-siddha gopis, who appeared on earth in order to serve Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who was both Radha and Krishna combined “Shri krishna-chaitanya, radha-krishna nahe anya”. Therefore by taking shelter of those acharyas in this disciplic line of the Gaudiya Goswamis is the same as taking direct shelter of the gopis of Vrindavana. This is the benediction of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, that the Gaudiya Vaishnava sampradaya has become manifested within the material world.

An important point for consider is that Shrila Narada Muni, the shiksa-guru of Lakshmiji, was the person who instructed Her to perform tapasya in Vrindavana; it was not Lakshmiji's own idea. Therefore Lakshmiji was right to follow the order of Narada, because no one can directly approach Radharani, or for that matter any of the gopis, who are all Radha's expansions. No doubt Narada Muni knew well the disposition of Lakshmiji as being situated in ashwarya-bhava and attached to the opulence and majesty of Vaikuntha, but regardless it was good for Lakshmiji to come to Belvana and meditate on Krishna's lotus feet and the rasa-lila pastimes. And besides that, Lakshmiji was also able to meet Krishna directly in Vrindavana.

Shrila Rupa Goswami, in his Laghu-bhagavatamrita, has quoted from the Padma Purana, where it is stated that Lakshmi Devi, the goddess of fortune, after seeing the beautiful features of Lord Krishna, was attracted to Him, and to get the favor of Lord Krishna She engaged herself in meditation. When asked by Krishna why She engaged in meditation with austerity, Lakshmi Devi answered, "I want to be one of Your associates like the gopis in Vrndavana." Hearing this, Lord Shri Krishna replied that it was quite impossible. Lakshmi Devi then said that She wanted to remain just like a golden line on the chest of the Lord. The Lord granted the request, and since then Lakshmi has always been situated on the chest of Lord Krishna as a golden line. In the Stavavali by Raghunatha Dasa Goswami it says, “Radha is the goddess resting on Lord Krishna's chest” The Brihad-Gautamiya Tantra, describes Radharani as being ‘sarva-lakshmi', or the ‘original source of all Lakshmis', "The transcendental goddess Srimati Radharani is the direct counterpart of Lord Shri Krishna. She is the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune. She possesses all the attractiveness to attract the all-attractive Personality of Godhead. She is the primeval internal potency of the Lord.”

## Part Nine: Philosophical Truths Regarding Shyamananda’s Tilak Pastime

With reference to Shyamananda finding the anklet of Radharani at Seva-kunja, which Lalita-sakhi asked him to keep secret, was because sahajiyas and other unqualified neophytes would simply misunderstand the significance of such a pastime, including his initiation, and flock to Vrindavana in the hope of seeing Radharani and the gopis at Seva Kunja. All the Gaudiya Goswamis were fortunate enough to have had similar transcendental experiences due to their being fully liberated souls and eternal associates (nitya-siddha) devotees of the Lord. However, the main aspect of their activities was preaching and distributing the holy name by spreading the sankirtana movement of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Shyamananda himself was one of the greatest preachers of the sankirtana movement and spent his whole life dedicated to serving Lord Chaitanya's mission. He personally inundated the state of Orissa with the sankirtana movement and converted thousands to the practice of Krishna-bhakti. There were many other miraculous events in his life and according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, he is the manjari named Kanaka in Krishna's Vrindavana pastimes.

Even today, it is widely believed that Radha and Krishna meet at Seva kunja every night for enjoying Their nocturnal pastimes. It is also said that anyone who dares to stay in Seva Kunja at night will go blind, go mad, or simply die. The pujari of the Rang Mahal Mandira at Seva Kunja even claims that many nice food preparations like sweets and other items are left there on silver plates for Radha and Krishna to eat during the night. The pujari claims that by the morning all the food preparations have been eaten and the plates are empty. A television crew even filmed the opening of the Rang Mahal temple in the morning and reported that only crumbs were left scattered on the ground. It so happened that this author also visited the Rang Mahal Mandira in the early hours one morning for taking photographs of Seva Kunja at dawn. As the pujari had not yet arrived, after peering inside the temple, scores of rats could be seen eating whatever food items had been left there by the pujari and by the time the pujari arrived only crumbs were left scattered on the ground by the rats.

The misguided neophytes, who congregate at places like Radha-kunda, and generally follow the artificial siddha-pranali process, usually end up indulging in illicit sex-life even if they have adopted grandiose titles like babaji, maharaja, or mahanta. The vast number of illicit liaisons amongst the babajis and protagonists of the siddha-pranali sampradaya, especially at Radha-kunda, is well known and has now become a part of the local folklore. The followers of siddha-pranali have been condemned by such great Vaishnava acharyas as Shrila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami as gross sentimentalists. Shrila Rupa Goswami in his celebrated book Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, says that siddha-pranali is simply a disturbance to the regular practice of sadhana-bhakti, or regulated devotional service. Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu never promoted, or even mentioned the system of siddha-pranali initiation anywhere in is teachings. He directly appointed Rupa and Sanatana to establish the bona-fide process of initiation according to the traditional Vedic system, which is exclusively based on the two simultaneous processes of Bhagavata-vidhi and pancharatrika-vidhi. The siddha-pranali process of initiation is in fact a non-Vedic tradition.

The other significant point to be understood from the tilak pastime is the great offence, or Vaishnava aparadha, in re-initiating disciples of another spiritual master. This unholy practice has now become prevalent in a large number of organizations including the Gaudiya Matha. If such an exalted nitya-siddha devotee like Hridaya Chaitanya, could be so disturbed and ready to challenge even the great Gaudiya Vaishnava acharya Shrila Jiva Goswami, it speaks volumes about the diabolical nature of this offence. Only after realizing the transcendental nature of Shyamananda's initiation, did Hrdaya Chaitanya become pacified. Due to committing such a serious Vaishnava aparadha, the spiritual advancement of those involved, either guru or disciple, is abruptly curtailed at least in this lifetime. The only condition mentioned in Vaishnava tantra for taking re-initiation, is when ones guru breaks the four regulative principles and falls down from his position and not otherwise. This provision is there because neophyte devotees (kanista-adhikaris), cannot comprehend that the line of disciplic succession is wholly dependent upon the Bhagavata-siksha parampara, rather than the Pancharatrika-diksha parampara.

Therefore in order to help such neophyte devotees retain their faith in Lord Krishna, they may be reinitiated.

## Part Ten: Shrila Narayana Bhatta - A Short Biography

According to the biographers of Shrila Narayana Bhatta, it is believed he was born in the year 1531, on the Narasimha-chatrurdasi day in the month of Vaishaka, into a Bhriguvamsa-dakhsinatya brahmana family at Madhurapattana in Andhra Pradesh. His father, Shriman Bhaskara Bhatta, was an erudite scholar and a devout Vaishnava devotee in the Brahma Madhava sampradaya, his mother's name was Yashomati Devi. In his early childhood he lived with his highly respected and learned uncle Shriman Shankara Bhatta, who was responsible for his education and tutelage in the Vedic scriptures. From his childhood he exhibited extraordinary intelligence as well as all the symptoms of a great devotee, he had no interest in material matters at all. He was such a brilliant student, that by the age of twelve he had mastered Sanskrit and studied all the important Vedic scriptures. Due to being inspired to live the life of a Vishnu-bhakta, he decided to leave his home and go on pilgrimage to the major holy place in India.

While still only twelve years of age, he started out on his pilgrimage and soon arrived at the river Godavari to take a holy bath. While on the banks of the sacred river, his biographers say that he suddenly went into a trance and had an ecstatic vision of Shri Shri Radha Shyamasundara standing before him. Shri Krishna spoke to him saying. “You are a partial expansion of my devotee Narada and you have been born for the purpose of rediscovering all the lost holy places in Vraja Mandala connected to My transcendental pastimes. My devotees Rupa and Sanatana have already found many of My 'lila-sthanas', but some are still remaining to be found.” Krishna then gave him a small Deity of Bala-Gopala named Ladalaya and said. “I am giving you this Deity of Ladalayaji, so serve Him with love and He will reveal to you all the secret pastime places in Vraja.” The word 'ladala' or ‘ladalaya' means 'adorable boy'.

After this transcendental experience on the banks of the Godavari, Narayana Bhatta started out on the long journey from Andhra Pradesh to Vrindavana along with his Deity Ladalayaji, eventually arriving in Vrindavana in the year 1545, at the age of fourteen. It took Narayana Bhatta almost two years to reach Vrindavana due to the influence of the Deity Ladalayaji, who guided Narayana Bhatta to visit all the holy tirthas and beautiful scenic places on the way to Vrindavana.

It is said that on his arrival in Vrindavana, he went immediately to meet Rupa and Sanatana Goswamis, who upon seeing him, understood he had been sent by the Lord to assist them in their work. They recommended that he stay with Krishna Dasa Brahmachari, a disciple of Gadadhara Pandita and assist him in his service as pujari of Lord Madana-Mohana. While accepting Rupa and Sanatana as his shiksha gurus, he eventually accepted Krishna Dasa Brahmachari as his diksha guru and learned from him the doctrines of 'Krishna-bhakti' as expounded by Lord Chaitanya and the Six Goswamis as well as the tenants and traditions of the Gaudiya Vaishnava sampradaya. He remained in Vrindavana for a number of years serving Shrila Sanatana Goswami's beloved Deity Lord Madana-Mohana.

After leaving the service of Lord Madana-Mohana, Narayana Bhatta moved to Radha-kunda and began in earnest his work of locating of the lost holy tirthas of Vraja not yet discovered by Rupa and Sanatana, or their associates. Traveling extensively around the entire

Vraja Mandala, he located every holy ‘tirtha' and 'lila-sthana' mentioned in the Adi-varaha Purana and could accomplish this task simply by the guidance of his Deity Ladalayaji. Narayana Bhatta visited each and every village in Vraja, and while there, he would meditate on his Deity Ladalayaji and the Deity would reveal to him where a particular holy tirtha was lying hidden. At that time, Raja Todarmal, the Finance Minister of Emperor Akbar, who was a devoted follower of Vaishnava Dharma, often provided the funds needed so that Shrila Narayana Bhatta, whom he respected as his guru, could construct memorials, rasa-mandalas and temples at the sites discovered by him.

Narayana Bhatta demarcated the geographic location of the twelve sacred forests of Vrindavana including all the upavanas, prativanas, and tapovanas, where Krishna's pastimes took place. He also discovered many of the sacred mountains and sacred kundas scattered around Vraja. He named every village after the pastime that had occurred there, just as Vajranabha had done four thousand years earlier. He also demarcated the exact boundary of the holy dhama and popularizeed the Vraja Mandala Parikrama that had been first inaugerated by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu during His pilgrimage to the holy Dhama in the year 1515.

One of the unique contributions of Narayana Bhatta was the discovery of the rasa-lila pastime places where he established at each place a circular platform known as a rasa-mandala to signify that the pastime of the ‘rasa-lila1 had occurred there. The sites of the ‘rasa-lila1 pastimes include such places as: Radha-kunda, Chandra-sarovara in Parasauli, Unchagrama, Viharavana, Kabambavana, Prema-sarovara, Mayur-kuti and a number of other celebrated sites. He also started the tradition of the ‘Krishna-lila' dramatic performances, known technically as the ‘rasa-lila nukarana' in which only young brahmana boys were allowed to enact the transcendental pastimes of Radha and Krishna. The brahmanas from the villages of Karhela and Pisawa, who are known as rasadharis, are the ones who organize and perform the rasa-lila dramas. The main disciple of Narayana Bhatta named Vraja-vallabha Dasa, was himself a good singer and musician and helped to develop this unique art form which is still very popular even today.

In the year 1553, Narayana Bhatta completed his most well-known book, the ‘Vraja-bhakti-vilasa', which details all the holy places within the holy Dhama of Vrindavana. The information in this important book forms an important basis for subsequent books written on the subject of Krishna's sacred pastime places in Vraja. After the publication of this book Narayana Bhatta received the honorary title of ‘Vraja-acharya'. The important Deities discovered and temples established by him includes; Larilylal Mandira at Varshana, Sanket Devi and Radharamana at Sanket, Dauji at Unchagrama, and Kameshwara Mahadeva at Kamyavana. Unfortunately, after his demise, his followers credited him with many discoveries that were originally made by the Rupa and Sanatana Goswamis.

After completing the Vraja-bhakti-vilasa, Narayana Bhatta moved to Unchagrama and absorbed himself in serving the Deity of Lord Balarama (Dauji). It is said that on the order of his father he accepted a wife and entered the ‘grihasta ashrama'. In time his son Damodara Bhatta became the head priest and pujari at the Larilylala Mandira at Varsana while his father remained as the pujari of the Dauji Mandira at Unchagrama. Even today, the priests of the Larilylala Mandira at Varsana are still initiated into the ‘diksha' line of Shrila Narayana Bhatta. There were at least sixty books written by Narayana Bhatta, but many of the original manuscripts were never found and thus were never published. His biographers say that he disappeared from the world in 1643, at Unchagrama where his samadhi has been established.

Unfortunately, some years after his departure, his followers began giving him the artificial title of ‘goswami', which is completely against the principles of Sanatana Dharma and contrary to the teachings of the Brahma Madhava sampradaya to which Narayana Bhatta belonged. The title goswami should only be adopted by a person who has renounced family life and has accepted the ‘sannyasa-ashrama', not a grihasta still serving his wife and children. In his own lifetime, Shrila Narayana Bhatta never announced that he was a ‘goswami' and would never allow anyone address him in such a manner. Those so-called brahmanas who fraudulently use the title ‘goswami', simply for their own false prestige, are condemned by the Vedic scriptures as ‘prakrita-sahajiyas', or persons who take religious matters very cheaply. Such sahajiyas who adopt the title of goswami as some kind of hereditary right are referred to as jati-gosai (castegoswamis) and are listed amongst the twelve deviant ‘apa-sampradayas' who have polluted the divine principles of Vedic culture and tradition.

## Part Eleven: Vallabhacharya and the Deity of Sri Nathaji

Vallabha Bhatta, who later became known as Vallabhacharya, is mentioned a number of times in the Chaitanya-charitamrita. He had the opportunity to meet Lord Chaitanya at both Puri and Prayag which is documented in Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya19, Antya7). Vallabha Bhatta was renowned as a great scholar and even wrote a commentary on the Shrimad-Bhagavatam. This particular commentary was not much appreciated by Lord Chaitanya as it did not follow the original Bhagavatam commentary of the revered Shridhara Swami, the first commentator on the Shrimad-Bhagavatam who appeared in the 8th century. Regarding this incidence, Shrila Prabhupada has said. “Among all commentaries, Shridhara Swami's is given the first position. This parampara has existed for a very long time. It was also accepted during Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's time, but Shri Vallabhacarya violated the system. Instead of acknowledging Shridhara Swami's pre-eminent position, he wanted to take it himself.”

**Vallabha Bhatta Meets Lord Chaitanya in Puri**

(Adapted From Chaitanya-charitamrita-Antya-lilach.7)

Vallabha Bhatta had arrived in Puri with the intention of presenting his commentary on the Shrimad-Bhagavatam before Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. However the Lord declined to hear anything from Vallabha Bhatta. Being omniscient, Lord Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu could understand that Vallabha Bhatta’s commentary on Bhagavatam and explanations of Krishna’s name were useless. Therefore He did not care about them. When Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu rigidly declined to hear his explanations; Vallabha Bhatta went home feeling extremely morose. His faith in the Lord and devotion to Him changed. Thereafter, Vallabha Bhatta went to the home of Gadadhara Pandita. He kept coming and going, showing affection in various ways, and thus maintained a relationship with him. Because Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu did not take Vallabha Bhatta very seriously, none of the people in Jagannatha Puri would hear any of his explanations. Feeling ashamed, insulted and unhappy, Vallabha Bhatta went to Gadadhara Pandita. Approaching him with great humility, Vallabha Bhatta said, “I have taken shelter of you, my dear sir. Kindly be merciful to me and save my life. Please hear my explanation of the meaning of Lord Krishna’s name. In that way the mud of the shame that has come upon me will be washed off.” Thus Pandita Gosai fell into a dilemma. He was in such doubt that he could not decide alone what to do. Although Gadahara Pandita Gosai did not want to hear it, Vallabha Bhatta began to read his explanation with great force. Because Vallabha Bhatta was a learned brahmana, Gadahara Pandita could not forbid him. Thus he began to think of Lord Krishna. “My dear Lord Krishna,” he requested, “please protect me in this danger. I have taken shelter of You.”

After some time, Vallabha Bhatta would go every day to the place of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu to engage in unnecessary arguments with Advaita Acharya and other great personalities, such as Svarupa Damodara. Whatever conclusions Vallabha Bhatta eagerly presented were refuted by personalities like Advaita Acharya. Whenever Vallabha Bhatta entered the society of devotees, headed by Advaita Acharya, he was like a duck in a society of white swans. One day Vallabha Bhatta said to Advaita Acharya, “Every living entity is female \[prakriti\] and considers Krishna her husband \[pot/\]. “It is the duty of a chaste wife, devoted to her husband, not to utter her husband's name, but all of you chant the name of Krishna. How can this be called a religious principle?” Advaita Acharya responded, “In front of you is Lord Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the personification of religious principles. You should ask Him, for He will give you the proper answer.” Hearing this, Lord Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu said, “My dear Vallabha Bhatta, you do not know religious principles. Actually, the first duty of a chaste woman is to carry out the order of her husband. The order of Krishna is to chant His name incessantly. Therefore one who is chaste and adherent to the husband Krishna, must chant the Lord's name, for she cannot deny the husband's order. Following this religious principle, a pure devotee of Lord Krishna always chants the holy name. As a result of this, he gets the fruit of ecstatic love for Krishna.” Hearing this, Vallabha Bhatta was speechless and returned home greatly unhappy and began to consider thus. “Every day I am defeated in this assembly. If by chance I am one day victorious, that will be a great source of happiness for me, and all my shame will go away. But what means shall I adopt to establish my statements?” The next day when he came to the assembly of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, he sat down after offering obeisances to the Lord and said something with great pride. “In my commentary on Shrimad-Bhagavatam,” he said, “I have refuted the explanations of Shridhar Swami. I cannot accept his explanations. “Whatever Shridhar Swami reads he explains according to the circumstances, therefore he is inconsistent in his explanations and cannot be accepted as an authority.” Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu smilingly replied, “One who does not accept the swami \[husband\] as an authority, I consider a prostitute.” After saying this, Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu became very grave. All the devotees present derived great satisfaction from hearing this statement. (Cc.Antya 7.88-116)

**Vallabha Bhatta Starts His Own Sampradaya**

It is said that within time, Vallabha Bhatta became initiated by Gadadhara Pandita. However, some time after this, being unable to fully comprehend the divinity of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu as an incarnation, and desiring to be recognized as a great acharya in his own right, Vallabha Bhatta left the Gaudiya Vaishnava sampradaya and joined the remnants of the Vishnuswami sampradaya in order to claim the vacant post of acharya. After some time, Vallabha Bhatta also deviated from the Vishnuswami sampradaya's theology and founded his own sampradaya, which he based on the doctrine of pushti-marga, where Krishna is worshiped as a child (Bala-Gopala). The word ‘pushti' means 'to nurture', or to 'gradually develop', one's devotional service. His adopting the pushti-marga theology was due to Vallabha's inability to fully comprehend the parakiya-rasa of Radha and Krishna as expounded by Lord Chaitanya. Vallabha also disregarded the importance of the maha-mantra and introduced his own mantra 'Shri Krishnah saranam mama' in order to distinguish himself as an acharya. Although the pushti-marga system established by Vallabha Bhatta is accepted by the Vaishnava community as a bone-fide practice, it is a very indirect process and is generally followed by householders who are considered to be on the level of karma-misra-bhaktas, or devotees still attached to family life. In the Vallabha sampradaya there is no recognition of vanashrama-dharma and thus there are no sannyasa or vanaprastha ashramas. Vallabha Bhatta made the worship of Bala Gopala, in the mood of vatsalya-bhava very popular amongst the followers of Hinduism and introduced two basic paths in the worship of Lord Vishnu. Maryada-bhakti, or devotion in reverence, where God is worshiped as the Supreme Brahman. The second being Pusthi-bhakti, or devotion in intimacy where God is worshiped in His form as a child.

When Vallabha Bhatta came on pilgrimage to Vrindavana, he travelled to many places around Vraja Mandala and gave discourses on his own subodhini commentary on the Shrimad-Bhagavatam. The places where he sat to give the discourse became known as Vallabha-baithaka or sitting place of Vallabhacharya. Unfortunately these bhaitaka's are now being called as Mahaprabhu's-baithaka, because the unscrupulous followers of Vallabhacharya have started calling Vallabhacharya as Mahaprabhu, in an attempt to make it appear that he was an incarnation and thus a rival to Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, which is simply fraudulent and creates confusion in the minds of innocent persons. The title 'Mahaprabhu' can only be used for a Vishnu-tattva incarnation like Lord Chaitanya and not for an ordinary jiva-tattva like Vallabhacharya, even if they do become sampradaya acharyas. Shrila Vallabhacharya never called himself Mahaprabhu, but according to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, he always addressed Lord Chaitanya as Mahaprabhu when he met Him in both Puri and Prayag. The renaming of Vallabhacharya as Mahaprabhu gained currency in the early seventies, after an article appeared in ISKCON'S 'Back to Godhead Magazine' with the episode mentioned in Chaitanya-charitamrita of Vallabha being rebuked by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu for attempting to supersede Shridhara Swami.

The followers of Vallabhacharya make all kinds of ridiculous claims regarding Vallabhacharya being an incarnation of Vishnu, but they cannot provide any reference from the Vedic scriptures to support their outrageous pronouncements, thus such fictitious claims must be summarily rejected by all intelligent persons. A genuine incarnation must find mention in the Vedas in order to be accepted as bona-fide. In the case of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu there are over a dozen references to His divinity found in the Vedas. Unfortunately, after Vallabha's death, his descendants who inherited the Vallabhacharya sampradaya, adopted the so-called jati-gosai, or 'caste-goswami system', in order to establish their hegemony over the innocent public, and thus regrettably became another apa-sampradaya. In the fraudulent jati-gosai caste system, all males born into such families are automatically given the goswami title whether they are qualified or not. The title goswami is meant only for those who have renounced all connection with material life in the form of family, friends, or society, not those who are married, or still attached to sex-life and the sensual pleasures of mundane existence.

During the British rule, the Vallabhacharya sampradaya became notorious when their 'so-called' goswami priesthood were involved in a number of highly publicized sex-scandals in Western India, which was been mentioned in the memoirs of the then District Magistrate of Mathura, R.S. Grouse. Regrettably, these deplorable episodes caused the British Government to adopt the view that all devotees of Krishna were simply debauchees and sex-mongers, and that Krishna was nothing more than a primitive tribal god. It was at this time that the British rulers felt it was their moral duty to expose the degradation of Hinduism and everything that it stood for, including the diabolical caste system. Consequently, due to the immoral activities of the Vallabhacharya sampradaya caste-goswamis, the whole of Hinduism was seen by the British rulers as a most degraded form of religion that should be eradicated from human society. Even quite recently the priesthood of the Vallabha sampradaya in Western India has been exposed to be still engaged in illicit sexual activities with their followers, which is most unbecoming of those who claim to be Vaishnavas - what to speak of their claim to be in the renounced order of goswamis.

## Part Twelve: Swami Haridasa and the Deity of Banke-Bihari

The history of Swami Haridasa, like other such histories of the period, is somewhat unclear. It is said that he was born in 1512, into a gaur-saraswata brahmana family at Kair, also called Kairwali Sarak near Aligarh. His family was originally from Multan in Punjab, which is now in Pakistan. The appellate ‘gaur-saraswata', or gaud-saraswata, signifies they were pancha-gauda, or North Indian Vaishnava brahmanas from the region formally known as Brahmavarta, which was situated on the banks of the River Saraswati. It is said these brahmanas migrated to various places like Saharanpura, Haridwara and as far south as Bengal in the distant past and are generally known by the name Pandey. There is another group of saraswata brahmanas with the appellate ‘gaud', who migrated to Southern India, who are not Vaishnavas, but are instead mayavadi impersonalist smartas who are found mostly in Karnataka and the Konkan regions of the sub-continent.

Swami Haridasa began his life as a professional musician mastering a variety of instruments and was also a noted singer of the classical dhrupad style. It is said that he was a disciple of the Karnataka musician-saint Purandhara, another famous exponent of dhrupad. He became a court musician at the Gwalior royal palace under the patronage of the Tomar Rajput kings and became part of celebrated Gwalior dhrupad gharana. The famous Hindustani classical singer, Miyan Tansen, whose real name was Ramtanu Pandey, was also a saraswata brahmana and court musician at Gwalior. Tensen accepted Swami Haridasa as his teacher and when Swami Haridasa decided to leave the royal court and dedicate his life to performing bhajana in Vrindavana, Tansen stayed with him for some time to continue his study of dhrupad. At this time Swami Haridasa became a follower of the Nimbarka sampradaya, which his father had also belonged to. It is interesting to note that there was a long standing tradition within the Nimbarka sampradaya for the dhrupad style of singing as far back as the 12th Century with Swami Sribhatta being one of the sampradaya's prominent exponents of dhrupad, who it appears Swami Haridasa was influenced by.

The dhrupad singing style is marked by a series of four line poetic verses set to a slow tempo and in a low register, being accompanied by the drone of a tampora and the beat of the mrdanga or pakhavaj. After leaving Vrindavana, Tansen, who was also a noted composer and rabab player, later accepted Muhammed Ghaus, the Sufi guru of the Gwalior gharana, as his spiritual and musical mentor. He eventually joined the Mughal court of Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri and is thought to have converted to Islam after marrying one of Akbar's daughters. His mausoleum was established next to his guru, Muhammed Ghaus at Fatehpur Sikri, after his death in 1586. Swami Haridasa was a contemporary of the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana but unfortunately, like Hit Harivamsa and Vallabhacharya, although they became part of the devotional bhakti cult spearheaded by Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, they could not comprehend Mahaprabhu's divinity or accept Him as an incarnation of Lord Krishna. Neither were they able to appreciate the sankirtana-yajna and propagation of the congregational chanting of the maha-mantra as the yuga-dharma.

Just like Hit Harivamsa and Vallabha Bhatta, Swami Haridasa also became the founder of his own religious sect and a competitor rather than a follower of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, He claimed that he was an incarnation of Lalita-sakhi, but there is absolutely no scriptural evidence to support such an outrageous claim. Unfortunately, it has become a tradition amongst the followers of some Indian saints to declare themselves as incarnations of some 'divine being' in order to enhance their reputation and following amongst the masses. The sect established by Swami Haridas is generally referred to as the Sakhi sampradaya, a sub-branch of the Nimbarka sampradaya. The 'so called' Sakhi sampradaya has adopted the diksha process known as siddha-pranali where sadhakas receive the name of a sakhi (gopi). However, the siddha-pranali system is not accepted by Shrila Rupa Goswami as an authorized Vedic process. Swami Haridasa was neither a scholar nor a philosopher and his followers do not have any authentic commentaries on the scriptures of their own. However, Swami Haridas is credited with writing a large number of devotional bhajanas that are still popular even today. Swami Haridas is also credited with discovering the Deity of Banke-Bihari at Nidhuvana where he performed his bhajana.

After the death of Swami Haridasa in 1575 (some say 1607), the Deity of Banke-Bihari was worshiped at Tattiya-sthan in Vrindavana by the ascetic followers of Haridasa's Sakhi-sampradaya. In the late 18th century, due to a rift amongst the followers of Swami Haridasa over the proprietorship of the Deity Banke-bihari, two separate groups emerged. The group who claimed descent from Haridasa's brother led by caste-goswamis (jati-gosai), eventually gained control over the Deity and forcibly moved the Deity of Banke-Bihari to the present location in Atthakambha, where a temple was eventually opened in 1862. Subsequently, this breakaway group of caste-goswamis claimed allegiance to the Vishnuswami sampradaya.

The Deity of Banke-Bihari is not one of the original Deities of Vrindavana established by Lord Krishna's great grandson Vajranabha Maharaja. The original name of the Deity appears to have been Bihariji until the late 18th century, when the Deity was moved to its present location in and the extra name Bake or Banke appears to have been added. The word 'bake', or 'banke', is supposedly derived from the word 'jhanke', or 'jhankiya', which means 'momentary,' or 'fleeting', and refers to the style of darshana which only lasts a few minutes, before a curtain is drawn by the pujari for a further few minutes, and then again reopened. This ritual of opening and closing of the curtain continues throughout the period that the temple is open and forms a part of the showmanship that sets this temple apart from all others. The same 'jhanke', or 'jhankiya', style of darshana can be seen at some temples in Mathura. The jhanakiya curtain ritual, as well as other aspects of the seva-puja, is irregular and not according to the Vedic standards or strict codes of traditional Deity worship mentioned in the Vedic shastras. At the Banke-Bihari temple there is no regular mangala-arati offering to the Deity. This is because the temple sevaks say, 'Banke-Bihari was out late at night enjoying nocturnal pastimes with the gopis in the groves of Vrindavana and therefore far too tired to get up in morning'. However such fraudulent claims are simply imaginative concoctions by the sahajiyas, which appeal to the ignorant and sentimental masses who have no understanding of Vedic scripture or tradition. There are also a number of other ridiculous and concocted stories apparently invented by the sevaks to attract the attention of the gullible public. In 1975, the ISKCON founder-acharya His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, forbade his disciples to visit this particular temple because it was managed by a sahajiya-sampradaya of caste-goswamis and their method of Deity worship and polluted brand of philosophy was not in accordance with the bona-fide Vaishnava traditions, thus by visiting such a temple his disciples might be influenced to become sahajiyas.

## Part Thirteen: Unscrupulous Claims of the Nimbarka Sampradaya

Unfortunately, followers of the Nimbarka sampradaya claim that many of the discoveries of the lost pastime places around Vrindavana Dhama made by the Gaudiya Goswamis were actually made by them. The Nimbarkas also claim that the Nimbarka sampradaya were the first to perform the dwadasa-vana Vraja Mandala Parikrama - and not Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Another claim is that one of the Nimbarka acharyas, the vairagi-baba named Srinagaji, was the first to write a book on the Vraja Mandala Parikrama some 30 years before Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's pilgrimage to Vraja, which took place in the year 1515. Needless to say, there is absolutely no historical evidence to substantiate such grandiose claims. Besides this, before the arrival of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and the Gaudiya Goswamis, all the sacred forests of Vraja, had not been discovered, this task was accomplished by Lokanatha Goswami and his close companion Bhugarbha Goswami after receiving the direct order From Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who sent the two Goswamis to Vrindavana in the year 1510. Similarly, almost all of the important holy places like Radha-kunda, Varsana and Nandagrama, to name a few, had not even been discovered until the arrival of Lord Chaitanya and his followers. The false claims of the Nimbarka followers surfaced just prior to the 500th anniversary of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's pilgrimage to Vrindavana, and at a time when ISKCON'S Vraja Mandala Parikrama had gained international recognition and was attracting thousands of pilgrims from around the world to take part in the parikrama, thus turning the annual Vraja Mandala Parikrama into a truly international event. The Nimbarkas are notorious for their exaggerated claims and in some accounts say that Nimbarkacharya was the first of the four Vaishnava sampradaya founders to appear, while claiming that he appeared sometime in the 6th century, followed by Vishnuswami, Ramanuja and Madhva. The truth is that Vishnuswami was the first of the sampradaya founders to appear taking birth in Southern India in the 3rd century BCE. Vedic scholars and historians are in agreement that Nimbarkacharya emerged around the 12th' or 13th century, making him the last of the Vaishnava sampradaya founders to appear.

Sadhu - a mendicant holy man

Sadhaka - one who follows a spiritual discipline under rules & regulations

Sakha - one of Krishna's intimate cowherd boyfriends

Sakhi - one of Radharani's intimate cowherd girlfriends

Sama Veda - a book of Vedic chants

Samadhi - the burial chamber or tomb of a great saint

Samadhi - a trance-like state of deep meditation, the last stage in ashtanga-yoga practice Sambhanda - love in direct association with Krishna

Samhita - a compilation of Vedic Knowledge

Sampradaya - an unbroken line of disciplic succession originating from Krishna

Sankirtana - the congregational or group chanting of the Lord's holy names

Sannyasi - one who has renounced all connection with family, home and society Seva - devotional service offered to the temple Deity or spiritual master

Seva-puja - the worship of the temple Deity

Shastra - any of the revealed Vedic scriptures.

Shiva - the avatar of Lord Vishnu in the mode of ignorance

Shringara - the decoration with ornaments and clothing of the temple Deity

Shringara-lila - the erotic decoration of Srimati Radharani by Krishna

Siddha-deha - one's eternal spiritual form

Siksha - instructions given by an advanced Vaishnava or guru

Siksha guru - the instructor spiritual master

Simhasana - the platform on which the Deity stands, or the seat of a great personality

Smriti - literally- 'that which is remembered' i.e. Vedic corollaries like the Vedangas & Puranas Sraddha - a Vedic ceremony honoring departed forefathers

Sruti - literally- 'that which is heard' i.e. Rig, Yajur, Sama & Atharva Vedas, Upanishads & Brahmanas

Swastika - An ancient Vedic symbol meaning: 'swaha' - auspicious offering & 'tika' - mark or symbol

**T**

Tapasya - voluntary acceptance of hardship and austerity for the purpose of purification

Tilak - the clay markings signifying Lord Vishnu seen on the body of a Vaishnava

Tirtha - a sacred or holy place where one can be purified of sin

**V**

Vaishnava - a devotee of Lord Vishnu or Krishna

Vamsi - Krishna's bamboo flute

Vana - forest

Vata - a banyana tree

Veda - knowledge of the Absolute Truth

Vedas - the four primarily samhitas i.e. Rig, Yajur, Sama & Atharva

Vedanta - literally 'the end of all knowledge'

Vedanta Sutra - the foremost exposition on Vedic knowledge

Vihara - intimate loving pastimes between Radha & Krishna

Vipralamba - love in separation from Krishna

Vraja - the innermost core of Vrindavana Dhama where Krishna performed His pastimes Vrajavasi - a resident of Vrindavana specifically during the time of Krishna's pastimes Vrata - a vow undertaken for spiritual advancement

**Y**

Yadava - a member of the Yadu Dynasty of ksatriyas in which Lord Krishna appeared

Yajna - a fire sacrifice or any other type of Vedic sacrifice approved by sashtra

Yajur Veda - a book of sacrificial formulae

Yaksha - an malevolent spirit and servants of the demigod Kuvera, the king of Yakshas

Yakshini - a female Yaksha generally considered as maidservants of Parvati

Yogamaya - the internal potency of Krishna

Yogamaya Devi - Krishna's sister also called Ekanamsa Devi

Yojana - an ancient Vedic measurement equal to about 8 miles

Yuga - an ancient Vedic division of time, the present age is known as Kali-yuga

Yutheshvara - a gopi who has her own group of younger gopi followers
